one_sentence: For MCI against controls from ADNI T1 MRI, P-109 reports 94.23% accuracy (AUC 0.9715) and P-66 reports 72.7% (AUC 0.80), a gap beyond combined uncertainty even at the smallest plausible test sets (z = 3.77); it counts as an unresolved discrepancy only on the literal reading of the Section 3.5 small-sample clause, because P-109's near-ceiling AUCs come from internal validation on randomly shuffled slices (about 50 per subject) with no external cohort, the leading candidate explanation alongside input representation, scanner subset and architecture.
reason: z = 0.2153/sqrt(0.0281^2+0.0498^2) = 3.77 at the most conservative n (6.01 with n = 400; AUC z = 3.19). Skeptic check: conditions 1-4 and 6 hold. On condition 5, P-109 meets three of four exclusion clauses from the source (AUC 0.9715/0.9852, internal slice-shuffled split, no external cohort), but its 1,075 participants (685 in the contrast) exceed every Section 3.5 exemplar and the review sets no cut-off, so the source does not establish the small-sample clause. The inputs differ within MRI: diffusion tensor/kurtosis white-matter indices against T1 slices.
The architectures differ: a balanced random forest against a CNN-transformer. On P-109's own split, CMT-T and DeiT-T score 74.87% and 79.96%.

one_sentence: For three-class CN/MCI/AD classification from ADNI MRI, a balanced random forest on diffusion indices reached 0.79 balanced accuracy under subject-level 5-fold CV in 150 participants (P-115), against 96.81% for a CNN-transformer on T1 slices under a random 10% slice-level hold-out from 1,075 participants (P-109) (z = 4.8; binary CN vs MCI 0.72 against 94.23%, z = 4.6). reason: z = 0.1781/sqrt(0.0333^2 + 0.0169^2) = 4.77. The pair stays robust with n = 96 (3.97), with slice-level n (5.34), with the plain-accuracy bound (2.07) and on the binary contrast (4.57). It came through reader and skeptic (challenge_skeptic_1), and I re-checked it against the correct P-115 document without finding a failed condition. P-109 escapes the Section 3.5 exclusion only because its sample is not small: its AUCs are 0.97 or more on internal validation with no external cohort, but it has 1,075 participants.

compared: No matched figure exists. Headline figures as recorded: random-forest AUC for AACD-defined MCI in CHARLS, P-27 training 0.826 against P-96 training set 0.93. I also tested P-27's internal (0.801) and CV (0.791) figures against 0.93, and the external figures (0.653 against 0.83/0.87).

The predictor sets differ: self-report variables (P-27) against education plus grip strength, anthropometry and routine blood values (P-96).
The label instruments differ: the HRS-style CHARLS battery (P-27) against a score P-96 calls the MMSE, both under an AACD definition.
The external cohorts differ: CLHLS scored with the CMMSE (P-27) against Yiwu 2021 and CHARLS 2011 (P-96).

P-96's Table 3 PPV and accuracy, its AUPRC and its external AUROC intervals all imply class-balanced (resampled) evaluation sets, although its text denies that SMOTE was applied to test or external sets. Its AUROCs may therefore be optimistic, but this is not shown to close the gap.

The CHARLS waves overlap, so the samples are not independent.
None is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: Two CHARLS random-forest models for AACD-defined MCI disagree: P-27 (older adults with depressive symptoms, self-report predictors) reported AUC 0.826 in training (0.801 internal, 0.653 external), against 0.93 in P-96's training set (0.83 and 0.87 external), whose predictors are education, grip strength, anthropometry and routine blood values (z = 7.8 on the training figures, over 12 on the external ones). The depression-restricted sample, the predictor sets, the label instrument and P-96's apparently class-balanced evaluation sets are candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient.
reason: z = 0.104/sqrt(0.0087^2 + 0.0102^2) = 7.77. The other tiers give internal 5.60, CV 9.75 and external 17.6 (12.7 with a Hanley-McNeil SE at the stated class sizes). The full skeptic check found no failed condition. Condition 1 is a judgement: the depressed sample is a subset of the same CHARLS community population, as in C-214 and C-265, and both are routine clinical tabular models whose top predictor is education, with the multimodal clause as in C-103 and C-188. The label-matched external figure widens the gap. Maximum AUC is 0.93, both papers validate externally, and the recorded figures are printed values. Correction to the advocate: P-96's external intervals are about half the Hanley-McNeil width at the stated class sizes and match balanced sets.

compared: No matched figure exists. Headline: MCI vs control AUC from structural MRI, P-52 test 0.864 (printed CI 0.73-0.89, 30/15) against P-99 0.735 (10-fold CV, 145/62). The record paired this with P-99's accuracy; AUC is compared here.

None is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For MCI versus controls from structural MRI, a hippocampal-radiomics XGBoost model reported test AUC 0.864 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.89) on a single 45-subject split (P-52), against 0.735 by 10-fold CV in 207 participants (P-99). The difference is marginal: z = 2.40 on the printed interval and 2.02 with a sample-size SE, but below 1.96 on other readings of P-52's asymmetric interval. P-52's tabulated control MoCA (22.5) also contradicts its stated control criterion (MoCA 27 or above).
reason: Under the brief's rule, z = 0.129/sqrt(0.0408^2 + 0.0351^2) = 2.40, and it is 2.02 with the Hanley-McNeil fallback. It falls to 1.95 with the exact binomial interval that matches the printed lower limit, and to 1.68 on the lower half-width alone; neither is the brief's method. In the skeptic check, the strongest attack is condition 1, P-52's control label. The source does not show whether the text or the tables are wrong, so the contradiction is carried as a label-definition candidate explanation, as in C-01. The other conditions hold. This is the narrowest pass in the batch.

The ledger's P-72 figure (94.61%) is P-72's AD vs NC accuracy, so it is not used.

b.se_source: No interval reported. The 70/15/15 subject-level split of 389 MCI gives about 57 test subjects per split (22 pMCI/35 sMCI, implied by Table 5: 15/22 and 29/35). Binomial SE sqrt(0.7368*0.2632/57) = 0.0583. The figure is a mean over 'three different subsets with different test sets' (p.6). If those test sets were disjoint, which the paper does not state, n = 171 and SE = 0.0337. AUC 0.721: Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0720 at 22/35, 0.0413 at 66/105.

candidate_explanations: Input representation and architecture: FreeSurfer DKT tabular features with a transformer (P-82) against a 3D CNN on CAT12 grey-matter maps (P-72).
Model selection on a small test set: P-82's 0.888 is the best of eight models scored on the same 24 subjects (AUC range 0.542 to 0.888).
Transfer initialisation in P-72: the conversion network starts from the AD vs NC weights ('we use the network parameters learned to initialize the training network for sMCI vs. pMCI task', p.6).
sMCI label: P-82 counts MCI reverters to normal as sMCI; P-72 states no minimum follow-up.
Class balance: 58% pMCI in P-82 against 39% in P-72.
Cohort selection: P-72 keeps only subjects with paired MRI and FDG-PET.
Evaluation design: one random 24-subject test set (P-82) against three held-out test sets of about 57, averaged (P-72). P-82's 10-fold CV is only in a supplement that is not available.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: On the matched condition (T1 MRI alone, conversion within 3 years in ADNI), P-82 reports 83.3% accuracy (AUC 0.888) on one 24-subject test set and P-72's MRI-only network reports 73.68% (AUC 0.721) averaged over three test sets of about 57. The accuracies do not differ beyond combined uncertainty (z = 1.01), and the AUCs reach z = 1.99 only if P-72's test sets are assumed to be disjoint, so the pair is not an unresolved discrepancy (the ledger's 94.61% for P-72 is its AD vs NC accuracy).
reason: Matched accuracy: z = 0.0965/sqrt(0.0761^2+0.0583^2) = 1.01, or 1.16 at n = 171. It fails. The AUC check gives 1.63 at the stated per-split class sizes and 1.99 only at the unstated disjoint 66/105. P-72's headline multimodal figure is closer still to P-82 (z 0.65 on accuracy, 1.33 on AUC). Full skeptic check: condition 1 holds (both are 3-year conversion in ADNI from baseline T1). Condition 2 holds. Condition 3 fails: P-72's MRI-only arm is a result under P-82's condition, and the matched accuracies agree within uncertainty at every plausible n. Condition 5 holds. Condition 6 fails for the ledger claim: the recorded 94.61% is P-72's AD vs NC result, and on the printed conversion figures the direction reverses. The advocate's one-directional exclusion is replaced by the uniform test, and C-80, the pair the advocate cited for consistency, also fails that test.

The headline multimodal figures, BA 0.733 (AUC 0.785) against BA 0.815 (AUC 0.874), mix PET with MRI plus metadata.

b.se_source: No interval reported, and the parenthesised fold variances were not used. 5-fold CV over 593 MCI (295 pMCI/298 sMCI). For the Cognitive-svm, BA = (0.75+0.79)/2 and SE = 0.5*sqrt(0.75*0.25/295 + 0.79*0.21/298) = 0.0173. AUC 0.832: Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0168. RFT: BA SE 0.0171, AUC SE 0.0168. MLP: BA SE 0.0177, AUC SE 0.0178.

scale: balanced accuracy (the ledger compares P-81's balanced accuracy); AUC as second check
candidate_explanations: Training target: P-81's conversion figures are zero-shot predictions from models trained on AD vs CN, while P-8 trains on the pMCI/sMCI labels.
Imaging modality in the headline models: FDG-PET (P-81) against T1 MRI plus FreeSurfer volumes (P-8).
Cognitive instruments: CDR-SB, logical memory delayed recall, MMSE and two mPACC composites (P-81) against MMSE, CDR-SB and ADAS-cog (P-8).
Additional predictors in P-8: sex, APOE4 and seven volumes. Its metadata-only SVM already reaches AUC 0.868.
Cohort and class balance: 36% converters with the FDG-PET restriction (P-81) against 50% (P-8). The ADNI subjects may overlap.
Label definition: P-8 requires the diagnosis to remain MCI for 36 months; P-81 labels all non-converters as stable.
Model and sample size in the cognitive-only arm: a dense network on 257 subjects (P-81) against SVM, RFT and MLP on 593 (P-8).
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: P-81 (FDG-PET, age and cognitive scores, zero-shot from an AD vs CN model) and P-8 (T1 MRI plus metadata) report 3-year conversion AUCs of 0.785 and 0.874 in ADNI. On the cognitive-score-only models that both papers report, the gap narrows to balanced accuracy 0.713 against 0.75-0.775 (z 1.12-1.89) and AUC 0.750 against 0.810-0.833 (z 1.61-2.25). The gap is therefore not established beyond uncertainty on the shared channel, and the pair is not reported as an unresolved discrepancy.
reason: Matched BA: z = 0.057/sqrt(0.0173^2+0.0279^2) = 1.74 for the SVM, 1.89 for RFT and 1.12 for MLP, and 1.58-1.89 for the SVM once the rounding of P-8's sensitivity and specificity is allowed for. All of these fail. The matched AUC check gives SVM 2.22, RFT 2.25 and MLP 1.61 (2.07/2.10/1.50 if P-81's CV pool excluded a 15% test hold-out). This is the one verdict that depends on the metric. On the ledger's metric the gap fails for every P-8 classifier, and P-8's own dense network on cognitive scores agrees with P-81's on both metrics, which fails condition 3. The headline figures differ (AUC z 2.57, BA z 2.51), but that comparison is not confined to the shared channel. The earlier skeptic check (challenge_skeptic_2) used the one-directional test.

Label definition: P-82 counts MCI-to-normal reverters as sMCI; P-3 requires the diagnosis to remain MCI.
Class balance and cohort: 58% pMCI (P-82) against 50% (P-3), on different ADNI subsets that may overlap.
Validation design: a single 24-subject test split, where one subject moves accuracy by 4.2 points, against 5-fold CV over 593.
P-3 tunes and selects its models on the evaluation folds. The authors say this biases P-3 upward, which runs against the gap.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: P-82 (83.3% accuracy, AUC 0.888, one 24-subject test set) and P-3 (74.61%, AUC 0.780, 5-fold CV over 593 subjects) both predict 3-year conversion from one baseline T1 MRI in ADNI. The difference is within combined uncertainty (z = 1.12 for accuracy, 1.43 for AUC) because P-82's estimate rests on 24 subjects, so the pair is not an unresolved discrepancy.
reason: Accuracy: z = 0.0872/sqrt(0.0761^2+0.0179^2) = 1.12. AUC: z = 0.108/sqrt(0.0729^2+0.0190^2) = 1.43. Both fail. The first pass and the skeptic qualified the pair only on the one-directional wording of condition 4. Conditions 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 hold, so the pair fails on the test alone.

compared: Headline figures (no matched figure exists): P-122 six-fold CV accuracy 84.28% (AUC 0.8599), from paired two-timepoint structural MRI, against P-3's 74.61% (AUC 0.780) from one baseline T1 scan. The task is pMCI vs sMCI in ADNI. P-122's hold-out figure of 84.74% is not used because it exceeds both its sensitivity (83.33%) and its specificity (82.27%).

a.se_source: The fold SD of 1.65 was not used. Binomial sqrt(0.8428*0.1572/275), with n = 275 subjects (121 pMCI/154 sMCI, 823 samples, p.5) as the conservative unit. On samples, SE = 0.0127 and z = 4.41. AUC 0.8599: Hanley-McNeil (121/154) SE 0.0236.

b.se_source: The fold variance was not used. Binomial with n = 593 subjects in 5-fold CV (p.6). AUC 0.780: Hanley-McNeil (295/298) SE 0.0190.

candidate_explanations: Two-timepoint longitudinal input (P-122) against a single baseline scan (P-3). P-122 does not state the interval between the scans, or whether the later scan comes before conversion.
Unit of analysis: accuracy over longitudinal samples (about three per subject) against one prediction per subject.
Input representation: 2D axial slice sequences against whole 3D volumes.
Label definition and cohort: DSM-5-guided selection from ADNI 1/GO/2/3 with no stated window, against dementia within 36 months in ADNI1/2.
Data augmentation in P-122.
P-3 tunes and selects its models on the evaluation folds, which biases P-3 upward, against the gap.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For pMCI vs sMCI from structural MRI in ADNI, P-122's model on two scans per subject reports 84.28% accuracy (AUC 0.860; six-fold CV, 275 subjects), against 74.61% (AUC 0.780; 5-fold CV, 593 subjects) for P-3's single-baseline-scan model. The gap is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 3.42 for accuracy, 2.64 for AUC), and neither paper reconciles it. Candidate explanations are longitudinal against single-scan input, sample-level scoring, 2D slices and label definition, and neither paper shows any of them to be sufficient.
reason: Accuracy: z = 0.0967/sqrt(0.0219^2+0.0179^2) = 3.42 (4.41 with samples as the unit). AUC: z = 0.0799/sqrt(0.0236^2+0.0190^2) = 2.64. Both pass. No matched figure exists: P-122's ablations all keep two timepoints. I re-read the conditions against the sources. Subjects are kept separate across subsets (p.6). The timing of the scans is unstated, so I cannot show that this is a different question. No figure is near 0.97. The ledger's 84.74% is the inconsistent hold-out figure, and the gap stands on the CV figure. The full skeptic check was done earlier in challenge_skeptic_2 and was not repeated here.

compared: pMCI vs sMCI accuracy in ADNI, MRI channel. Matched figure: P-72 sMRI-only arm 73.68% (baseline sMRI, Table 2) vs P-122 six-fold CV 84.28% (longitudinal two-timepoint sMRI). The recorded 94.61% is P-72's AD-vs-NC figure and is not used.

a.se_source: No interval; SD 1.65 is a fold spread, so SE from n = 275 subjects (154 sMCI + 121 pMCI): sqrt(0.8428*0.1572/275) = 0.0219. On 823 samples it would be 0.0127.

b.se_source: No interval; each test set is 15% of 389, i.e. 57 subjects (22/35; 77.19% = 44/57): sqrt(0.7368*0.2632/57) = 0.0583. The paper does not say the three 'different test sets' are disjoint, so pooled n = 171 (SE 0.0337) is not used as primary.

scale: accuracy (proportion); AUC checked as a sensitivity
candidate_explanations: Longitudinal two-timepoint input (P-122) vs baseline-only images (P-72). P-122 p1: 'The architecture synthesizes longitudinal sMRI data from dual temporal points'.

Unit of analysis: longitudinal samples, about three per subject (P-122), vs one prediction per subject (P-72). P-122 p5: 'For the sMCI group, we gathered 449 longitudinal samples from 154 subjects diagnosed with sMCI.'
Test-set design and size: mean of three 57-subject test subsets (P-72) vs six-fold CV over 275 subjects. P-72 p6: 'construct three different subsets with different test sets'.

Input representation: 2D axial slice sequences (P-122) vs 3D volumes (P-72). P-122 p8: 'This discrepancy may be attributable to their utilization of 3D MRI images, while we used 2D image sequence processing strategy.'
Label definition and class balance: AD within 3 years, 39% pMCI (P-72) vs DSM-5-guided selection with no stated window, 45% pMCI samples (P-122).
PET fusion in P-72's headline model. Its sMRI-only figure is lower (73.68%), so fusion does not account for P-72 being lower.
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For predicting MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI from structural MRI, P-122 reports 84.28% accuracy (six-fold CV, longitudinal MRI, 275 subjects) and P-72 reports 77.19% with MRI plus PET, or 73.68% with MRI alone, on 57-subject test sets. The gap is within combined uncertainty (z = 1.70 on the MRI-only figure), so it is a difference in reported accuracy, not a reportable conflict.
reason: Matched: z = 0.1060/sqrt(0.0219^2+0.0583^2) = 0.1060/0.0623 = 1.70. Other constructions: 1.78 on P-122's samples; headline 77.19 gives 1.19; matched AUC 0.721 vs 0.8599 (Hanley-McNeil 22/35 and 121/154) gives 1.83; headline AUC gives 1.44. The pair passes only if P-72's three test sets are pooled as 171 disjoint subjects (2.64 matched accuracy; break-even n = 80). That pooling is not established. The paper says only 'different test sets'. Its printed SD of 1.01 across the three subsets cannot arise from three 57-subject accuracies averaging 44/57 (the smallest non-zero SD is 1.75), and it is far below the roughly 5.6-point sampling SD that disjoint sets would show. Conditions 1-3, 5 and 6 were upheld earlier (challenge_skeptic_2); only condition 4 fails.

compared: MCI vs CN accuracy in ADNI from T1 MRI. Matched figure: P-66 amygdala-only radiomic+CNN fusion 70.0% (Table 6) vs P-125 mean test accuracy 80.00% (RF/ANN, 8 amygdala features). P-125's abstract 82.14% is not in its results tables.

a.se_source: The printed +/-2.43% is a 95% MOE across five fold-models on one test partition (RF recall 92.86 +/- 0), which is a fold spread, so SE from n. Test n = 28 is implied (recall 13/14; '3.6 % of MCI as HC' = 1/28), or 30 from the 60-40 split: sqrt(0.16/28) = 0.0756 (0.0730 at n = 30).

b.se_source: The printed +/-1.6 is an SD across five repetitions on one fixed 20% image test set, so SE from n of about 252 distinct subjects (about 360 test images from 948+853): sqrt(0.21/252) = 0.0289 (0.0242 at 360).

scale: accuracy (proportion); AUC checked as a sensitivity
candidate_explanations: Features within MRI: 8 amygdala morphometric scalars vs 1746 radiomic features per ROI fused with 3D-CNN features. P-125 p8: 'used for training were V, VN, DC, and TR for both hemispheres of the amygdala, for a total of 8 features.'
Participant selection: strict ADNI criteria in P-125 (HC MMSE 28-30, CDR 0) vs 200 randomly selected per group in P-66.
Test-set size: about 28-30 subjects (P-125) vs about 360 images from about 250 subjects (P-66).
Split unit: subject-level (P-125) vs image-level (P-66). The leakage this allows would favour P-66, so it runs against the gap.
Classifier and ROI set: RF/SVM/KNN/ANN on the amygdala vs radiomics+CNN fusion over hippocampus and amygdala.
None of these is shown to be sufficient; P-66's amygdala-only arm moves away from P-125.
one_sentence: For MCI vs cognitively normal classification from T1 MRI in ADNI, P-125 reports 80.00% test accuracy from eight amygdala measures on about 28 held-out subjects, against 72.7% for P-66's radiomics-CNN fusion and 70.0% for its amygdala-only arm. The gap is within combined uncertainty (z = 1.24 on the amygdala-matched figures, 0.91 on the headlines), mainly because P-125's test set is so small.
reason: Matched: z = 0.100/sqrt(0.0756^2+0.0289^2) = 0.100/0.0809 = 1.24, and 1.24-1.30 across plausible n. Headline 80.00 vs 72.7 gives 0.91-0.95. AUC: RF 85.71 vs 77.5 gives 1.06. Even the best-of-four SVM 90.31 against P-66's lowest arm (77.5) gives 1.95, below 1.96. P-125's printed MOE is a spread among fold-models on one partition, not an SE. This is one of the five pairs the operator named, and it was judged by the same test. Conditions 1-3, 5 and 6 were upheld earlier (challenge_skeptic_3); condition 4 fails.

compared: Binary MCI vs HC accuracy in ADNI from T1 MRI: P-109 BrainViT-L 94.23% (random 90/10 split of shuffled slices) vs P-125 80.00% (subject-level test partition). No matched figure exists. The recorded 96.81% is P-109's three-class figure and is not used.

a.se_source: No interval. The test set is 10% of about 34,000 shuffled slices, about 50 per subject, so nearly all 685 contrast subjects (370 MCI + 315 HC) contribute: sqrt(0.9423*0.0577/685) = 0.0089. At n = 69 it is 0.0281; on about 3,400 slices, 0.0040.

b.se_source: The printed +/-2.43% MOE is a fold spread on one test partition, so SE from n = 28 (implied by the printed metrics) or 30: sqrt(0.16/28) = 0.0756 (0.0730).

scale: accuracy (proportion); AUC checked as a sensitivity
candidate_explanations: Split unit: random slice-level split, so one subject's slices can sit in both training and test sets (P-109), vs subject-level hold-out (P-125). P-109 p8: 'The images were shuffled randomly, and all experiments were carried out by splitting the data into 10 % for testing and 90 % for training.'
Input representation: about 50 2D slices per subject classified individually vs 8 amygdala scalars per subject.
Sample size: 685 subjects in the contrast vs 74, with about 28-30 test subjects in P-125.
Architecture: CNN-transformer hybrid on images vs classical classifiers on hand-crafted features.
Participant selection and acquisition: P-125 restricts controls to MMSE 28-30 and CDR 0; P-109 uses 3 T scans and states no criteria beyond ADNI diagnosis.
None of these is shown to be sufficient; the split unit is the leading candidate.
one_sentence: For binary MCI vs healthy-control classification from T1 MRI in ADNI, P-109 reports 94.23% accuracy (AUC 97.15%) from a vision transformer tested on a random 10% of shuffled slices, so the same subjects appear in training and test, while P-125 reports 80.00% from eight amygdala measures on about 28 held-out subjects. The difference does not exceed combined uncertainty under any construction (z = 1.87; at most 1.95), and P-109's slice-level split is the leading candidate explanation.
reason: z = 0.1423/sqrt(0.0089^2+0.0756^2) = 0.1423/0.0761 = 1.87. Every construction is below 1.96: 1.77-1.88 at P-125 n = 28 and 1.82-1.95 at n = 30. Even with zero SE for P-109, z is only 1.88 or 1.95, because P-125's 28-30 test subjects alone carry an SE of 0.073-0.076. AUC 0.9715 vs 0.8571 or 0.9031 gives 1.50 or 1.07. The advocate's 'both directions' result rested on P-125's fold-spread MOE and on the superseded one-sided wording. Skeptic check: (1) holds; (2) holds; (3) holds, no matched figure; (4) fails; (5) contested but not shown failed on the letter. P-109 meets the ceiling limb (AUC 97.15/98.52) with internal validation only, calls its data 'only a small amount of ADNI Alzheimer's data', and evaluates on shuffled slices. But its 685 subjects exceed every Section 3.5 exemplar, and C-46 read P-109 the same way. (6) holds once the binary figure replaces the three-class one. The pair fails on condition 4 whichever way condition 5 is read.

compared: MCI-to-AD/dementia progression AUC in ADNI from cognitive and MRI data. Matched: P-168 single-timepoint random forest 0.90 (month-24 exam) vs P-156 Ensemble Integration test AUC 0.81 (baseline data only). Headline P-168 LSTM: 0.93.

a.se_source: +/-0.09 is a fold SD, so Hanley-McNeil on n = 347 (77/270): Q1 = 0.818, Q2 = 0.853, SE = 0.0242. The LSTM 0.93 gives 0.0206.

b.se_source: No interval. Test set = 841 - 672 = 169. The class split is not printed, so it is estimated from the cohort's 286/841 = 34% as 58/111: Hanley-McNeil SE 0.0377 (0.0399 at 50/119, 0.0359 at 66/103).

candidate_explanations: Horizon: fixed 2 years from a month-24 index exam (P-168) vs latest recorded diagnosis (P-156). P-156 p4: 'The most recent diagnosis given to each patient (Final DX) was the outcome predicted'.
Cohort construction: P-168 is complete-case, five visits, still MCI at month 24, and excludes 187 with undetermined status at month 48; P-156 takes all 841 baseline EMCI/LMCI.
Index timepoint: P-168's single-timepoint model uses the month-24 exam, not the first MCI visit. The longitudinal effect it quantifies (0.03, DeLong P = 0.039) explains only part of the gap.
Validation optimism in P-168: hyperparameters were tuned by 10-fold CV on the same 347 participants that were later scored by 10-fold CV.
Validation design: 10-fold CV mean (P-168) vs a single random 20% held-out test set (P-156).
Feature loss and processing in P-156: PET and DTI were dropped for missingness, and TADPOLE merges ADNI editions.
Label and case mix: AD vs dementia; 35.4% of P-156's cohort is early MCI.
None of these is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For predicting progression from MCI to AD or dementia in ADNI from cognitive and MRI data, P-168 reports AUC 0.90 from a single-timepoint model (0.93 with five visits; 10-fold CV, 347 participants, 2-year horizon), and P-156 reports AUC 0.81 from baseline data on a 169-patient held-out set. The matched figures differ only just beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.01), a margin that depends on P-156's unprinted test class split. Horizon, cohort selection, index timepoint and validation design are candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient.
reason: Matched: z = 0.090/sqrt(0.0242^2+0.0377^2) = 0.090/0.0448 = 2.01, which passes. Headline 0.93 vs 0.81 gives 2.80 (2.67-2.90). The pass is thin, for three reasons. First, z falls below 1.96 if P-156's test set held 52 or fewer progressors (1.93 at 50/119), which has about an 18% chance under a random 20% draw (mean 57.5, SD 5.5). Second, the figures are printed to two decimals, and a difference below 0.088 would fail. Third, a fold-SD-as-SE construction would give 1.91, but the brief directs deriving the SE from n. The age-restricted AUCs of P-168 are subsets and not the matched figure. Conditions 1-3, 5 and 6 were upheld earlier (challenge_skeptic_3), and the source figures were spot-checked here. The ADNI samples overlap, so the two studies are not independent.

compared: Accuracy for MCI vs controls from resting electrophysiology. The recorded conversion claim is a misreading: 94.76% is P-129's specificity, and P-129 has no conversion analysis. P-173 NC vs stable MCI (mean of 10 classifiers, 5-fold CV, n=101) against P-129 MCI vs HC (subject-wise nested CV, n=61). No matched figure exists. NC/sMCI is taken as the P-173 figure nearest P-129's MCI group, which is not selected by course: sMCI is 48 of P-173's 76 MCI, and its 48:53 class balance is nearer P-129's 32:29 than NC/pMCI's 28:53.

a.se_source: No interval printed (p. 9). n = 101 (53 NC + 48 sMCI): sqrt(0.79*0.21/101) = 0.0405. NC/pMCI 0.82, n = 81: SE 0.0427.

b.se_source: The printed +/-0.60% is an SD over 20 seeds, not a sampling interval. n = 61 subjects (32 MCI + 29 HC): sqrt(0.9097*0.0903/61) = 0.0367.

candidate_explanations: Classifier averaging (P-173): 'we averaged the classification accuracy of ten popular classifiers' (p. 7), against one tuned transformer in P-129.
Course-defined subsets (P-173): sMCI n=48 and pMCI n=28 defined by outcome at about 3 years (p. 4).

Population and MCI definition: P-173 has 'MCI due to AD' with hippocampal atrophy, Hachinski <= 4 and no infarction, against relatives and volunteers as controls. P-129 has 'subjects admitted to the cardiac catheterization units at Sina and Nour Hospitals', with MCI defined by MMSE 21-26.
Unit of analysis (P-129): accuracy over 2-s epochs (14,420 MCI / 16,282 HC epochs), not per subject.
Features and validation: alpha-band MEG MG2G embeddings with 5-fold CV, against raw 19-channel EEG into a transformer with nested CV repeated 20 times.
Age 65-80 against over 55.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: P-173 (Madrid MEG, mean of ten classifiers) reports 79% accuracy for controls vs stable MCI (82% vs progressive MCI), and P-129 (Isfahan EEG from cardiac catheterization patients) reports 90.97% for MCI vs controls. The gap exceeds combined uncertainty only on the stable-MCI contrast (z = 2.19; 1.59 on the progressive one), and the samples come from different population classes. The ledger's conversion claim is a misreading. The pair is not reported as a discrepancy.
reason: Condition 1 fails on population class. P-129's sample (both groups) comes from cardiac catheterization admissions, with MCI defined by an MMSE band. P-173 studies vascular-screened 'MCI due to AD'. A disease-defined patient sample against Alzheimer's-spectrum MCI matches the rule's Parkinson's example, read as in C-172. Conditions 2, 3, 5 and 6 hold. z = 0.1197/0.0547 = 2.19 on NC/sMCI, but 0.0897/0.0563 = 1.59 on NC/pMCI, so the gap is also fragile. If the operator reads population class as the MCI construct alone, the pair would qualify on NC/sMCI.

compared: Accuracy for MCI vs controls from resting electrophysiology. The recorded conversion claim is a misreading: P-153 has no conversion analysis. P-173 NC vs stable MCI (n=101) against P-153 Dataset I MCI vs healthy (mean of three random 41/20 subject splits). No matched figure exists. NC/sMCI is the nearer P-173 contrast, as in C-95.

a.se_source: No interval printed. n = 101: sqrt(0.79*0.21/101) = 0.0405. NC/pMCI 0.82, n = 81: SE 0.0427.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Each split tests '20 subjects (9 MCI and 11 healthy)' (p. 4): sqrt(0.9396*0.0604/20) = 0.0533. At n = 60 pooled predictions, SE = 0.0308.

candidate_explanations: Classifier averaging (P-173): the figure is a ten-classifier mean (p. 7).
Selection on the evaluation splits (P-153): component number R, the 1.5-min patch and the 60 bands were all chosen by best accuracy (p. 10).
Course-defined subsets (P-173): sMCI/pMCI by outcome at about 3 years.
Dataset and hardware: the same P-153 pipeline gives 93.96% on Dataset I and 78.65% on Dataset II (p. 1).
Unit of analysis unclear (P-153): 93.96% is not a mean of three 20-subject vote accuracies, and Table 5's sensitivity 96.07% and specificity 96.98% imply about 96.6%.
Sample size and validation: three random 20-subject test sets from 61 subjects, against 5-fold CV on 81-101 subjects.
Population and MCI definition: 'MCI due to AD' aged 65-80, against MMSE/NUCOG-defined MCI over 55 on the Isfahan dataset, which P-129 describes as cardiac catheterization admissions.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: P-153 reports 93.96% accuracy for MCI vs healthy controls on the Isfahan EEG dataset that P-129 also uses, against P-173's 79% (controls vs stable MCI) and 82% (vs progressive MCI). z is 2.24 and 1.75 at P-153's 20-subject test sets, the samples come from different population classes, and P-153's figure is inconsistent with its own sensitivity and specificity. The pair is not reported as a discrepancy; if it were, it would be one discrepancy with C-95.
reason: Condition 1 fails for the same reason as C-95. P-153's Dataset I is the same public Isfahan dataset (Ref. [24], Noor Hospital, 61 subjects over 55, MMSE 21-26 / NUCOG 75-86.5, 19 channels, 256 Hz, 30 min), which P-129 describes as cardiac catheterization admissions. P-153's own text does not mention the cardiac units. Conditions 2, 3, 5 (0.9396, best split 0.9652 and implied 0.966 are all below 0.97) and 6 hold. z = 0.1496/0.0669 = 2.24 on NC/sMCI. NC/pMCI gives 1.75 at n = 20 and passes only from n = 30. If population class is read as the MCI construct alone, the pair would qualify on NC/sMCI and should be merged with C-95.

compared: ROC-AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI: P-178 9-feature random forest (early MCI, open horizon, 95 test patients) against P-185 MRI subspace biomarker with SVM (ADNI-1, 3-year conversion, 10-fold CV x20). No matched figure exists. AUC is used because converter prevalence differs (12.8% vs 57%). The recorded accuracies give the same result.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil at subject level for 95 test patients. The class split is not printed, so about 12 converters / 83 non-converters is taken from the ratio 49/383: Q1 0.923, Q2 0.940, SE 0.040 (0.049 at 8/87).

b.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with 126 pMCI / 95 sMCI: Q1 0.533, Q2 0.570, SE 0.0349.

candidate_explanations: Predictor set: P-178 adds ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE, age, race and APOE4 to two MRI volumes; P-185 uses MRI only. P-178's 6-feature model without MRI or APOE4 still reaches AUC 0.88, but P-178 has no MRI-only model.
Label and horizon: last-visit diagnosis (open horizon) against conversion within 3 years.
Population and prevalence: ADNI-GO/2 early MCI with 49/383 converters against ADNI-1 MCI with 126/221.

Unit of analysis and evaluation (P-178): oversampled visit records from one random split. Table 1 (balanced 402/402 test set) contradicts Table 4, which implies an imbalanced test set with about 56% of converter visits identified.
Model selection on test accuracy (P-178): the nine-feature group was chosen because 'our accuracy rose to 93.6%'.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: P-178 reports AUC 0.96 (accuracy 93.6%) for predicting conversion of ADNI early MCI to AD from cognitive scores, APOE4, demographics and two MRI volumes. P-185 reports AUC 0.6951 (accuracy 69.37%) for 3-year conversion in ADNI-1 MCI from MRI morphometry alone. The gap exceeds combined uncertainty (z = 4.99) and neither paper explains it; the candidate explanations are the non-shared cognitive predictors, the open horizon and early-MCI population, and P-178's visit-level oversampled single-split evaluation.
reason: Figures and class sizes were re-checked in the sources. z = 0.2649/0.0531 = 4.99 at conservative subject-level class sizes (4.41 at 8/87, 6.61 at 49/334). Accuracy z = 6.07. The pair already passed the reader and challenge_skeptic_3 with no failed condition: condition 1 holds through the multimodal clause, as in C-154 and C-188, and 0.96 is below the 0.97 exclusion. The full skeptic check was therefore not repeated. The pair qualifies.

compared: ROC-AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion within 36 months in ADNI-1, with MRI shared. No matched figure exists. P-186 prints two headline AUCs of equal standing (0.912 at 6 months ahead, 0.957 at 1 year ahead). The ledger cites 0.957 and the registry 0.912. The 6-month arm is nearer P-179's single baseline visit and 125 subjects: it uses two readings 6 months apart plus a forecast, 119 subjects, against 85 in the 1-year arm. It is therefore the compared figure.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with 49 MCIp / 70 MCIs: Q1 0.838, Q2 0.870, SE 0.0297. The 1-year 0.957 (35/50) has SE 0.0249.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Class sizes from Table 1: 39/48 sensitivity, 60/77 specificity, 99/125 accuracy. Hanley-McNeil 48/77: Q1 0.704, Q2 0.747, SE 0.0406.

candidate_explanations: Input representation (P-186): its authors attribute the AUC to 'the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion'. This is asserted, not tested.
Non-shared predictors: neuropsychological measures in P-186 (MRI-only 0.905 / 0.88) against blood SNP and mRNA in P-179.
Subset-size selection on AUC: both P-186 figures are the maximum over marker-subset sizes. P-179 also chose its feature number by AUC.
Preprocessing outside the folds (P-186): features were scaled before the train-test split.
Outcome window (P-186): MCIp means conversion any time before month 36, so an early converter's observed readings can fall at or after conversion.
Eligible sample: 85 or 119 subjects with complete consecutive readings, against 125 with baseline blood omics.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: P-186 reports AUC 0.957 (1 year ahead, 85 subjects) and 0.912 (6 months ahead, 119 subjects) for 36-month MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI-1, against 0.826 in P-179 (125 subjects, baseline MRI plus blood omics). Only P-186's best figure differs beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.75). Its analysis nearest P-179's design (z = 1.71), its MRI-only arms (z = 1.45 and 1.02) and the two papers' accuracies (81% or 84.9% against 79.2%) do not. The pair is not reported as a discrepancy.
reason: In the skeptic check, conditions 1, 2, 3 (as written), 5 and 6 hold. Condition 4 fails on the compared figure: z = 0.086/0.0503 = 1.71 (1.93 with Hanley-McNeil class roles swapped). The ledger's 0.957 gives z = 2.75, but it is P-186's single most favourable analysis: the maximum over marker subsets, on the arm with the most follow-up input and the smallest sample. If the operator takes 0.957 as the compared figure, every condition holds and the pair qualifies at z = 2.75.

compared: pMCI vs sMCI in ADNI from structural MRI. There is no matched figure, so the headline figures are compared. P-182: accuracy 0.7585 (AUC 0.777) on 381 test subjects. P-122's headline of 84.74% is an aggregate of its held-out split and its CV, and it exceeds both its own sensitivity (83.33%) and specificity (82.27%), so it cannot come from one confusion matrix. P-122's six-fold CV result over all 275 subjects is used instead: accuracy 0.8428 (AUC 0.8599). AUC z = (0.8599-0.777)/sqrt(0.02765^2+0.02365^2) = 2.28. The headline with n=275 gives z = 2.88.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial sqrt(0.7585x0.2415/381) = 0.02193, with n = 381 (118 pMCI/263 sMCI, p.2). The printed sensitivity 0.66 and specificity 0.8 give 0.757, which is consistent.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial sqrt(0.8428x0.1572/275) = 0.02195, with n = 275 subjects in the six-fold CV (121/154, Table 1; splits keep each subject in one subset). The printed '+-1.65' is the fold mean minus the lowest fold, a spread across folds, not an SE.

candidate_explanations: Architecture: P-122's multi-scale attention and fusion modules. Its own ablation (unimproved Eff-GCNet 71.6%, AUC 0.7770) uses P-122's own input, label and target, not P-182's condition, so it is not shown to be sufficient for the gap between the papers.
Input: two time points (P-122) vs one baseline scan (P-182: 'we did not examine longitudinal changes in imaging metrics').
Input region: P-182 uses only a 3D box around the hippocampus.
Training target: P-182 trains on AD vs CN and transfers to MCI.

Label window: P-182 requires evaluations at least 18 months apart and excludes 65 reverters. P-122 gives no window beyond 'guided by DSM-5 criteria', and it does not say whether the later scan precedes conversion.
Unit of analysis and validation: P-122 scores samples and aggregates both validation schemes. Its ablation tables fit a 102-case test set (42/60), not the stated 124.
Single modality, which P-182 names as possibly lowering its performance.

one_sentence: For progressive versus stable MCI from structural MRI in ADNI, a hippocampal-box DenseNet trained on AD versus controls reached 75.85% accuracy (AUC 0.777) on 381 subjects (P-182), and a two-timepoint whole-brain CNN-Transformer reached 84.28% in six-fold CV over 275 subjects (AUC 0.860; headline 84.74%) (P-122). The gap is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.72) and unexplained, and its candidate explanations have not been tested.
reason: z = 0.0843/sqrt(0.02193^2+0.02195^2) = 2.72, and AUC z = 2.28. Skeptic check: conditions 1, 2, 5 and 6 hold on the sources. Condition 3 holds: neither paper prints a result under the other's condition, and P-122's ablation keeps its own condition. That ablation rests on a 102-case test set, and the module effect is within uncertainty at subject level. Fragility: on P-122's held-out split alone, z = 1.00-1.58, so the verdict depends on the CV figure. The record should cite 84.28% rather than the internally inconsistent 84.74%.

compared: MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI from MRI plus cognitive tests, AUC. There is no matched figure: P-186 has no baseline-only arm and P-183 has no longitudinal arm. P-183 ENS 0.824 (CI 0.681-0.968, n=40) is compared with P-186 NM+MRI 1-year 0.957 (n=85). With P-186's 6-month 0.912, z = 1.11.

one_sentence: A baseline T2-map plus neuropsychology ensemble reached AUC 0.824 (95% CI 0.681-0.968, n = 40) (P-183), and a longitudinal forecast model reached AUC 0.957 one year ahead (n = 85) (P-186). The difference is within combined uncertainty (z = 1.72), so the pair should not be reported as an unresolved discrepancy.

compared: Conversion from MCI to AD/dementia in ADNI from cognitive tests plus FreeSurfer MRI, AUC. There is no matched figure. P-186 NM+MRI 1-year 0.957 (5-fold CV, n=85) is compared with P-156 EI 0.81 on a held-out test set of 169 patients. With P-186's 6-month 0.912, z = 2.13.

Outcome window: before month 36 (P-186) vs the most recent diagnosis with no fixed horizon (P-156).

one_sentence: For predicting conversion from MCI in ADNI from cognitive and MRI measures, a longitudinal forecast model reached AUC 0.957 one year ahead (5-fold CV, n = 85) (P-186), and a baseline-only multimodal ensemble reached AUC 0.81 on 169 held-out patients (P-156). The difference is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 3.26) and unexplained, and the candidate explanations are not shown to be sufficient.
reason: z = 0.147/sqrt(0.0249^2+0.03766^2) = 3.26. The alternatives also pass (6-month z = 2.13; 57/112 split z = 3.24). The sources support conditions 1-3, 5 and 6: 0.957 is below 0.97, P-186's ground-truth AUC of 0.98 is not the compared figure, and nothing reconciles the pair. The report should note that P-186's 0.957 is optimistic.

compared: Three-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI from baseline T1 sMRI, accuracy. There is no matched figure. P-207 CFMnetwork 0.8772 (10-fold CV, n=234) is compared with P-185 0.6937 (20x10-fold CV, n=221). The ledger's 90.44% is P-207's AD-vs-NC figure and is not used.

Condition 5 holds (below 0.97). Condition 6 holds on the printed 87.72%. Sensitivity: at P-207's grid median z = 1.52. Parameter choice is recorded as a candidate explanation, and C-117 is ruled on the same basis.

one_sentence: At the matched three-year horizon, the MRI-based model of Cai et al. (P-211; regional MRI measures with demographics and APOE4, no cognitive tests) reached a cross-validated AUC of about 0.70 (read from its Figure 2d), below the AUC of 0.827 that Bae et al. (P-37) report for a 3D CNN on baseline T1 scans (z = 2.2, a narrow margin), which reverses the recorded comparison (0.92 vs 0.827, which set P-211's five-year figure against a three-year one and cited the P-174 duplicate stub).
reason: z = |0.827 - 0.703| / sqrt(0.0498^2 + 0.0254^2) = 0.124/0.0559 = 2.22 (2.24 with the full 188/392). Skeptic check: (1) holds: both predict 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI amnestic MCI through MRI, and the differences are allowed; (2) holds, AUC; (3) holds on the best-matched figure, since Comb (c) is the only 3-year P-211 figure without the cognitive channel P-37 does not use. But P-211's 3-year figures that add cognitive scores agree with 0.827 (test-set Comb (a) 0.81, z = 0.21; CV Comb (a) 0.753, z = 1.34), so the verdict rests on treating Comb (c) as the governing matched figure, as in C-151; (4) passes narrowly: z = 2.04 at 0.713 and 1.92 at 0.72, so it depends on the plot read-off being accurate to about 0.01; (5) holds, all < 0.97; (6) holds only once the record is restated: the 0.827 is Bae et al. (P-37), not the P-174 stub, and the ledger's 0.92 is a five-year figure (headline z = 1.72 would not pass). So the qualifying gap runs opposite to the record, with P-211 lower. I could not show a failed condition; this is the thinnest margin in the batch.
candidate_explanations: Label definition: P-37 keeps later converters and short-follow-up MCI out of the stable group ('MCI subjects with a duration of MCI less than 3 years without conversion were excluded due to the potential possibility of near-future conversion.'). P-211's 3-year negatives include later converters, and P-211 attributes its 3-year dip to them ('these false positives represent individuals whose diagnostic classification did not change during the short-term follow-up period, despite the disease progressing and eventually reaching the dementia stage at a later time point'). It prints no 3-year AUC with them removed.
Input representation and model: ten FreeSurfer regional measures plus covariates in an EBM (P-211) against a transfer-learned 3D CNN on the whole T1 image (P-37).
Pretraining (P-37): 'The source task used 1406 DAT and 2084 NC scans from 1080 subjects.' P-211 trains on MCI only.
Validation design: one random 68-scan held-out test (P-37) against 5-fold CV with SMOTE (P-211: 'All EBMs were tested with the 5-fold cross validation.').
Index scan and cohort: P-37 uses 'the single time point sMRI scan at which an individual first received a diagnosis of MCI'; P-211 uses the ADNI baseline visit of amnestic MCI from ADNI1/2/3/GO.
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient.

compared: Matched figure at P-93's condition (36-month conversion, neuroimaging only): P-211 Comb (c) 3-year 5-fold CV AUC (Figure 2(d)) against P-93's MCI-conversion AUC 0.838 on an independent MRI-only ADNI test set. scale: ROC AUC; SE by Hanley-McNeil from class sizes
one_sentence: For three-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, Liu et al. (P-93) report AUC 0.838 on an independent MRI-only test set, while the MRI model without cognitive scores of Cai et al. (P-211) reaches about 0.70 in cross-validation (read from its Figure 2d; z = 3.4), the reverse of the recorded 0.92 vs 0.838, which set P-211's five-year multimodal figure against a 36-month one.
reason: z = |0.838 - 0.703| / sqrt(0.0310^2 + 0.0254^2) = 0.135/0.0401 = 3.37. Robust to the read-off (2.96 at 0.72) and to the choice of CV figure (Comb (a) CV 0.753 gives z = 2.17). Test-set composition (P-93): 96 pMCI/81 sMCI in the text against 93/66 in Tables 2 and 5.

None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient.

one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, Guan et al. (P-229) report AUC 0.757 from grey-matter volumes alone, with a classifier trained only on AD/NC labels, against AUC 0.96 for the random forest of Velazquez and Lee (P-178), which combines two MRI volumes with cognitive scores, APOE4 and demographics in early MCI over an open horizon (z = 4.3). P-178's figure is visit-level, its feature set was chosen on its test split, and its tables disagree on the test-set size.
reason: z = |0.96 - 0.757| / sqrt(0.040^2 + 0.0252^2) = 0.203/0.0473 = 4.29 (4.16 at 11/84). No matched figure exists. 0.96 < 0.97, so condition 5 passes by the letter. The record's misread 71.05% is set aside under condition 6.

Horizon and label: conversion by the last visit (mean 5.02 years) in P-178 against within 36 months in P-229.
Training design (P-229): the MCI subjects are an unlabelled target domain, with AD/NC as the labelled source.
Population: early MCI only (P-178) against unselected ADNI MCI (P-229).
Unit of analysis and reporting (P-178): visit-level training and testing; the Table 1 test count (402/402) contradicts Table 4.
Model selection on the test split (P-178): 'by removing the RAVLT features, our accuracy rose to 93.6%'.
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient.

compared: No matched figure exists, so the printed headline conversion figures are compared (the record misreads both): P-229 IADT MCI-to-AD accuracy 73.54% (Table IV) against P-207 CFMnetwork MCI-c vs MCI-nc accuracy 87.72%. Accuracy, because P-207 reports no AUC.

b.se_source: No interval printed. 87.72%, 10-fold CV over 126 MCI-c + 108 MCI-nc = 234. SE = sqrt(0.8772 x 0.1228/234) = 0.0215; Wilson [0.829, 0.913].

scale: accuracy (proportion); binomial SE from the evaluation-set n
one_sentence: For three-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI from structural-MRI grey-matter volumes, Liu et al. (P-207) report 87.72% accuracy (10-fold CV, 234 MCI) with a coupled network representation, against 73.54% for Guan et al. (P-229) on 393 MCI with a classifier trained only on AD/NC labels (z = 4.6). The two papers' plain regional-volume baselines coincide (64.15% and 64.12%), which points to the methods, but neither paper reports a figure under the other's conditions.
reason: z = 0.1418/sqrt(0.0223^2 + 0.0215^2) = 4.59. Skeptic check: (1) holds: 3-year conversion in ADNI MCI from baseline sMRI GMV; (2) holds, accuracy on near-balanced sets; (3) is the only contestable condition. The baseline coincidence (64.12 vs 64.15) sets a logistic regression on 90 AAL volumes trained on AD/NC against AdaBoost-SVM on ICA-network ROIs trained on MCI labels, so it is not a figure under the other's condition. P-207's plain features (64.15%) also fall below P-229's reported 73.54% beyond uncertainty (z = 0.0939/sqrt(0.0314^2 + 0.0223^2) = 2.44), so the ablation does not show the representation alone reconciles the reported figures. I could not show condition 3 failed. (5) holds, both < 0.97; the E1/E2 setting was fixed on AD vs NC, which weakens the best-of-15 concern; (6) the misread record figures are set aside, and the printed conversion figures still disagree. Qualifies, on the same reading of the sufficiency clause as C-147, which the operator may overrule.
candidate_explanations: Feature representation (P-207): 'The best classification accuracies for different features are 64.15% for OFMROI, 75.10% for CFMROI, 68.62% for OFMnetwork, and 87.72% for CFMnetwork.'
Training design: P-229's classifier never sees MCI labels (AD/NC source, unlabelled MCI target); P-207 trains on MCI labels by 10-fold CV.
Parameter selection (P-207): E1 and E2 searched over {2,3,4} x {1..5}; the AD/NC-chosen setting is also the MCI maximum, and the other settings give 70.24-82.31%.
Label definition: P-207's MCI-nc are 'otherwise', with no minimum follow-up stated, against P-229's 36-month stable group.
Region set and sample: the top 3 ROIs per AD/NC-derived ICA network on 234 MCI (P-207) against 90 AAL regions on 393 MCI (P-229).
Coupling weights (P-207) are computed across subjects, and the paper does not say this was done inside the training folds.
None of these is shown by either paper to be sufficient for the cross-paper gap.

one_sentence: On MRI alone, in ADNI MCI with 5-fold cross-validation, P-239's radiomics branch predicts time to AD conversion with a C-index of 0.67 against 0.756 for P-241's S-CNN (z = 2.5; P-241's other MRI models give 0.73-0.75, two within uncertainty of 0.67). reason: The full skeptic check of conditions 1-6 found no failed condition. P-241 also prints its S-CNN under P-239's cohort and design (ADNI, 5-fold CV), and that fully matched figure (0.756) differs from P-239's 0.67: z = 0.086/0.0339 = 2.54, or 2.39 if P-239's 0.67 is taken as 0.675. The margin is modest. It rests on Hanley-McNeil SEs for a censored C-index, with the event count derived from rounded censoring rates. P-241's CPH (z 2.35) and Weibull (2.14) models also clear the test, but its two MLPs (1.77, 1.71) do not. The pair qualifies as a discrepancy in the direction opposite to the record.

compared: No figure at a matched horizon exists: P-198's AUC is for conversion by about 2 years, and P-244 prints only 1/3/5/10-year time-dependent AUCs. Neither paper has the other's predictor set. So the headline figures are compared: P-244 5-year 0.957 (recorded; abstract) vs P-198 0.78. Bracketing: 1y 0.810 agrees (z 0.6-0.9), 3y 0.914 differs (z 4.5-5.4), interpolated 2y 0.862 differs (z 2.4-2.9).

a.se_source: No interval or per-horizon class sizes printed. HM at an assumed conservative 100/100: Q1 0.9175, Q2 0.9360, SE 0.0148, CI [0.928, 0.986]; at a plausible 300/110, SE 0.0091.

scale: ROC AUC: time-dependent AUC at t (P-244) vs binary AUC for conversion within about 2 years (P-198)
candidate_explanations: Predictor set: P-244 'concatenated the baseline clinical features and neuroimaging features extracted from the MRI scans'; P-198 uses five cortical-thickness covariates only. P-244 has no MRI-only arm.
Horizon: P-198 predicts transition 'within the next two years'; P-244's AUC rises with horizon, and its 1-year 0.810 agrees with P-198.

Possible internal optimism in P-244: internal MMSE AUCs are 0.537-0.600, but in AIBL (30 MCI) the Deep-AD C-index is 0.752 against MMSE's 0.730, and the external AUCs are described only as 'consistently comparative performance with MMSE'.
Time conditioning in P-244 training (q(z|x,t)); the paper says inference uses 'data x at the starting point' only.

Inclusion and follow-up: P-244 requires at least two MRI scans and follows up to 10 years with censoring; P-198 requires a follow-up scan about 2 years after baseline.
P-244's SEs rest on assumed per-horizon counts.
None is shown by either paper to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, P-244 reports time-dependent AUCs of 0.957 at 5 years and 0.914 at 3 years, against P-198's 0.78 for conversion within about 2 years. P-244's own 1-year AUC (0.810) agrees with P-198, so the gap may be partly a horizon effect as well as P-244's added cognitive predictors, and neither paper reports a result at the other's horizon.
reason: The full skeptic check found no condition failed as the rule is written. Condition 1 holds through the multimodal clause, as in C-103 and C-188. Condition 3 holds because no figure exists at P-198's horizon and neither paper shows the horizon or the predictor set to be sufficient. Condition 5 holds: 0.957 < 0.97, n = 783, there is an external AIBL cohort, and the methods place AUC under five-fold CV. The headline test passes easily (z 6.79). At P-198's horizon, though, the result rests on interpolation: the 1-year figure agrees and the 3-year figure does not. The concave printed series puts the 2-year value near 0.86, outside P-198's interval (z 2.4-2.9 under assumed counts). The pair qualifies but is fragile. The report must give the horizons and say that P-244's 1-year figure agrees with P-198.

compared: Matched input: P-69 headline Model 5 Interaction-Based ResBlocks (demographics + driving, I-score selected) vs P-331 Model 4 (demographics + driving). The comparison uses balanced accuracy derived from the printed counts, because raw accuracy is prevalence-confounded: an all-healthy rule scores 90/105 = 0.857 in P-69's test set. scale: Balanced accuracy (0-1), derived from printed counts; both papers print accuracy
candidate_explanations: Class mix and operating point: 14% vs 61% impaired; P-331 selects models by F1 ('optimizing the balance between precision and recall'); P-69 tests on 90 healthy and 15 impaired drivers.

I-score selection carries the gap. Without it, P-69's RF (BA 0.700, z 0.74), ResBlocks (0.767, z 1.58) and logistic regression (0.778, z 1.75) on the same inputs are within uncertainty of P-331. The modules come from 'Applying BDA to the dementia dataset', with no stated hold-out of the test cases.

one_sentence: Among older drivers, P-69's naturalistic-driving model separates cognitively impaired from healthy drivers with 96% accuracy (balanced 0.87, on 15 impaired and 90 healthy test drivers). P-331 reaches 67-69% (balanced 0.64-0.67) on the same demographics-plus-driving inputs. reason: This was not an advocate-only pair. Its skeptic check was done in challenge_skeptic_4 (no failed condition) and is not repeated in full; this round re-read the printed counts and ran the test. Balanced accuracy 0.867 vs 0.643 gives z = 0.2239/0.0725 = 3.09 (headline Model 6: z 2.74; one-year-ahead: z 2.37), so the pair qualifies. The report must say two things. First, raw accuracy is inflated by P-69's 86% healthy test set. Second, the gap depends on I-score selection, which is not shown to exclude the test cases.

compared: Horizon-matched: P-244 3-year time-dependent AUC 0.914 vs P-356 36-month AUC 0.74 (ViT on hippocampal T1 slices). No input-matched figure exists in either paper. The record's 5-year 0.957 is replaced by the matched 3-year figure.

a.se_source: No interval or per-horizon counts printed. HM at one fold's size (about 70 cases / 87 controls of 783 MCI / 348 converters): Q1 0.8416, Q2 0.8729, SE 0.0248, CI [0.865, 0.963]. Across assumptions the SE ranges from 0.0111 (348/435) to 0.0362 (30/127).

candidate_explanations: Predictor set: P-244 adds cognitive/clinical scores and APOE4 to FreeSurfer morphometry; P-356 'solely focused on MRI features'. P-244 has no MRI-only model.
Estimand and censoring: time-dependent AUC over all MCI with 55.56% right censored (P-244) vs a cleaned dichotomy (P-356). The cleaning favours P-356, so it does not explain P-356's lower figure.

Time conditioning in P-244 training; the paper says inference uses baseline x only.
