one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD progression in ADNI, P-244's clinical-plus-MRI survival model reports a 3-year time-dependent AUC of 0.914, against 0.74 for P-356's hippocampal-slice vision transformer at 36 months (z = 2.9). Candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient, are P-244's added cognitive and APOE4 predictors, its survival estimand and its unprinted external AUCs.
reason: This was not an advocate-only pair. Its skeptic check was done in challenge_skeptic_4 (no failed condition) and is not repeated in full. On the horizon-matched figures, z = 0.174/0.0594 = 2.93. It stays at or above 2.68 under every assumed P-244 class size (3.16 at 348/435), and P-356's best run (0.78) still gives z 2.15-2.59. The pair qualifies. P-244's SE rests on assumed counts.

compared: MCI prevalence among community-dwelling older adults as each paper prints it (P-259: 194 MCI of 902 assessed; P-261: 314 MCI of 1,071 analysed). No matched figure exists: P-259 has no prevalence for ages 60-75 or under MoCA cut-offs, and P-261 has none under a consensus Petersen/DSM-5 diagnosis or above age 75. The ledger's pairing (prevalence against the joint-exposure OR of 2.581) is a misread, so under condition 6 the printed prevalences are judged.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial sqrt(p(1-p)/n), p = 194/902, n = 902 (696 normal, 194 MCI, 12 dementia; p.5): sqrt(0.2151x0.7849/902) = 0.01368. With the 12 dementia cases removed (194/890): 0.01384.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial, p = 314/1071, n = 1071 (p.3 'Among the 1071 study subjects, 314 suffered from MCI, with a prevalence rate of 29.3%.'): sqrt(0.2932x0.7068/1071) = 0.01391.

one_sentence: Two community samples of older adults report different MCI prevalences: 21.5% (194 of 902; Singapore, ages 60-99, Petersen criteria with a consensus panel) and 29.3% (314 of 1,071; Fuzhou, ages 55-75, non-depressed, MoCA-based). The gap is well beyond sampling uncertainty (z = 4.0). Differences in diagnostic procedure, sampling frame and country could explain it, but neither paper shows that they do. The ledger's pairing of the prevalence with an odds ratio of 2.581 is a misread.
reason: z = 0.0781/sqrt(0.01368^2+0.01391^2) = 4.00 (3.83 with dementia cases removed). A design effect above about 4 in both studies would be needed to bring z below 1.96. The skeptic check against both source texts found no failed condition as the rule is written. The strongest objection is to condition 1. P-261's aims concern sleep and Qi-stagnation, so its 29.3% describes a restricted analysed sample (non-depressed, ages 55-75, able to care for themselves, 58.8% of those recruited). On the other side, P-261 sized its sample with a prevalence formula (permissible error 3%). Cohort and label differences are allowed. Condition 2 names prevalence against prevalence, and the brief's own example class is community older adults. The objection is therefore recorded as a caveat, not as a failed condition. The advocate's overturn of the reader's borderline verdict stands. Age band and depression handling run against the gap.
candidate_explanations: Diagnostic operationalisation: MoCA cut-offs (P-261) against Petersen criteria, 1.5 SD below norms on any test and a consensus panel (P-259). P-259 says its broad battery raises its own estimate, which runs against the gap.
Sampling frame: random draws from the health records of 34 day-care centres in Fuzhou (P-261) against door-to-door and word-of-mouth recruitment in western Singapore (P-259).
Response and missing-data exclusions in P-261: 1071 (58.81%) of the 1821 recruited were analysed.
Sample restrictions in P-261: ages 55-75, self-care ability, GDS-15 > 8 or a history of depression excluded. P-259 took ages 60-99 and included non-ambulant participants. Age runs against the gap.
Country and population: Singapore against Fuzhou, China. P-259 cites a range of 5-36.7% under a uniform criterion.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.

compared: Headline AUC for MCI-to-AD conversion from baseline T1 MRI in ADNI: P-41's CNN ensemble reaches 0.9287 on one held-out test split (15 sMCI / 15 pMCI+AD). P-65's HemiNet reaches 0.8401 on 573 subjects under five-fold stratified CV repeated five times. No matched figure exists.

a.se_source: The +/-3.58 on a single split is undefined. Hanley-McNeil on the test classes 15/15 (Table 1 'Test 15 15'): Q1 = 0.8669, Q2 = 0.8944, SE^2 = 0.5743/225, SE = 0.0505 (0.0535 at the abstract's 0.92).

b.se_source: The +/-0.0297 is an SD across runs. Hanley-McNeil on 300 pMCI / 273 sMCI: Q1 = 0.7243, Q2 = 0.7671, SE^2 = 22.35/81900, SE = 0.0165.

one_sentence: P-41 reports an AUC of 0.93 (0.92 in its abstract) for MCI-to-AD conversion on a 30-subject ADNI test split. P-65 reports 0.84 on 573 ADNI subjects under repeated five-fold cross-validation. The gap lies within their combined sampling uncertainty (z = 1.67), so the pair is not an unresolved discrepancy.
reason: z = 0.0886/sqrt(0.0505^2+0.0165^2) = 1.67 < 1.96. The result is robust: z = 1.75 even with P-65's SE set to 0, and 1.43 at P-41's abstract value of 0.92. The first pass qualified the pair only on the one-directional interval reading. challenge_skeptic_5 found no other failed condition. It noted that P-41's accuracy of 91.77% is inconsistent with its sensitivity of 87.69 and specificity of 88.53 on balanced classes.
candidate_explanations: P-41 added 15 patients already diagnosed with AD to its positive class.
Horizon: conversion between M18 and M48 (P-41) against within 36 months (P-65).
Validation: one 30-subject test split on which more than a dozen configurations were scored and the best reported (P-41), against repeated five-fold CV on 573 subjects (P-65).
P-41's printed metrics are internally inconsistent, and its evaluation unit is unclear.
2D multi-plane slices in a CNN ensemble (P-41) against a whole-volume 3D asymmetry CNN (P-65).
Cohort selection: 192 subjects chosen by data availability (P-41) against 573 right-handed subjects only (P-65).

compared: Headline accuracy for predicting NC-to-MCI progression in ADNI from baseline hippocampal MRI: P-132's LightGBM reaches 0.74 on the test set (26/35; radiomics plus ADAS-Cog; 7-year horizon). P-177 reaches 0.92 on ADNI under leave-one-out (60 progressors to amnestic MCI, 60 matched non-progressors; about a 2-year horizon). No matched figure exists. The ledger's 'Acc 79' is P-132's training accuracy.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial on a test set of 25 sNC + 10 pNC = 35: sqrt(0.7429x0.2571/35) = 0.0739.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial on the ADNI LOOCV set of 60/60 = 120: sqrt(0.92x0.08/120) = 0.0248. The Table 5 SD of 0.01 is a spread, not an SE.

one_sentence: For predicting progression from normal cognition to MCI in ADNI from baseline hippocampal MRI, P-132 reports a test accuracy of 0.74 (26 of 35; 7-year horizon; 25 stable to 10 progressors). P-177 reports 0.92 (leave-one-out over 60 amnestic-MCI progressors and 60 matched non-progressors; about a 2-year horizon). The gap is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.27). Horizon, the extreme-group matched design, class balance, features and validation are candidate explanations, and neither paper shows any of them to be sufficient.
reason: z = 0.1771/sqrt(0.0248^2+0.0739^2) = 2.27; 2.23 with 110/120 and 2.34 with 111/120. The margin is modest and depends on which figure is taken. P-132's SVM (0.77) gives 1.98, or 1.93 against 110/120. P-177's patch-selection mean (0.90) gives 1.99. The headline pair passes. challenge_skeptic_5 checked the reader+skeptic route and found no failed condition. P-177's 0.97 is a specificity, and its dictionary is unsupervised.
candidate_explanations: Horizon: 7 years (P-132) against about 2 years (P-177).
Extreme-group design: amnestic-MCI progressors against matched non-progressors unimpaired for at least 4 years (P-177), against all NC with 7-year follow-up (P-132).
Scan timing conditioned on outcome: P-177 took progressor scans 2 years before decline.
Class balance: 25:10, with printed F1 implying almost no progressors detected (P-132), against 60:60 (P-177).
Features: radiomics plus ADAS-Cog (P-132) against surface morphometry with sparse coding (P-177). P-177's volume baseline scores 0.72 in its own design.
Validation and size: a 35-subject held-out split (P-132) against LOOCV on 120 (P-177), with small samples named as a limitation.

compared: MCI vs healthy controls in ADNI from MRI. Matched figures: P-152's superficial-white-matter DTI SVM gives 83.3% (40/48), AUC 0.88, under internal 5-fold CV. P-63's T1 MRI-only arm gives 70.08%, AUC 76.41%, under 10-fold CV on 158 CN / 128 MCI. The ledger's 95.8% (AD vs HC) against 76.88% (CN vs MCI) compares different contrasts and is set aside under condition 6. On AD vs CN and MCI vs AD the two papers agree.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial with n = 48 (24 MCI / 24 HC, CV over the contrast): sqrt(0.8333x0.1667/48) = 0.0538. AUC 0.88 by Hanley-McNeil 24/24: SE 0.0511.

b.se_source: The +/-3.49 is an SD across folds. Binomial with n = 286 (158 CN + 128 MCI): sqrt(0.7008x0.2992/286) = 0.0271. AUC 0.7641 by Hanley-McNeil 128/158: SE 0.0288.

one_sentence: For MCI versus healthy controls in ADNI from MRI, P-152 reports 83.3% accuracy (AUC 0.88) from superficial-white-matter DTI features on 48 subjects. P-63's T1 MRI-only arm reports 70.08% (AUC 0.764) on 286 subjects. The gap narrowly clears combined uncertainty (accuracy z = 2.20; AUC z = 1.98). P-63's fused genetic-plus-MRI model (76.88%, AUC 0.873) does not differ from P-152 (z = 1.09).
reason: Accuracy z = 0.1325/sqrt(0.0538^2+0.0271^2) = 2.20. AUC z = 1.98 depends on the rounding of '.88' (1.86 at 0.875), so accuracy carries the result. The pass depends on the MRI-only arm being the matched figure; against the fused headline, z = 1.09. Skeptic check: condition 1 holds (the MRI channel is shared; P-63's separate ADNI 'MCI' label is an allowed difference). Condition 5 holds on the compared figures, the convention used for C-211 (same P-152 table), C-66 and C-117. A study-level reading would fail P-152 on its AD-vs-HC AUC of 0.99, and would fail C-211 as well. On condition 6, P-152 prints 83.3% as the MCI-HC accuracy four times. An undefined 'Correction' column (70.3) and a sensitivity/specificity pair that cannot come from one confusion matrix are reliability concerns, not a demonstrated misreading. The advocate's overturn stands, on a thin margin.
candidate_explanations: Features within the MRI channel: SWM DTI tract, connectivity and network features (P-152) against whole-brain T1 (P-63).
FCBF feature selection before the internal 5-fold CV (P-152).
Best kernel chosen per contrast on the same CV (P-152).
Label definition: P-63 keeps ADNI 'MCI' separate from EMCI/LMCI because the diagnostic criteria differ; P-152's MCI come from ADNI2.
Sample size and cohort: 48 ADNI2 DTI subjects, with small sample size named as a limitation (P-152), against 286 subjects with complete SNP/GE/MRI data (P-63).
Reporting reliability in P-152: the undefined 'Correction' value of 70.3 and a sensitivity/specificity pair inconsistent with the printed accuracy.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.

compared: AD vs MCI from MRI in ADNI, AUC of each paper's best model: P-152 Gaussian-kernel SVM on superficial-white-matter DTI features (Table 3) against P-301 ROI-3DViT-DBN ensemble on T1 regional volumes (Table 3). No matched figure exists.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with 24 AD/24 MCI ('72 subjects: 24 subjects as HC, 24 subjects with MCI, and 24 subjects with AD'): Q1 = 0.869, Q2 = 0.896, SE = sqrt([0.0651 + 23(0.0043) + 23(0.0314)]/576) = 0.0392.

b.se_source: No interval or validation n printed (80/20 split, results on the validation set). n derived as 20% of 117 AD + 247 MCI = about 72 (23/49). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.429, Q2 = 0.450, SE = sqrt([0.24 + 22(0.069) + 48(0.090)]/1127) = 0.0734; at n = 50, SE 0.0883.

one_sentence: On AD versus MCI from MRI in ADNI, P-152 (diffusion MRI, 24 AD/24 MCI, 5-fold CV after feature selection) reports AUC 0.93 and P-301 (T1 MRI, 80/20 split of 364 AD+MCI scans) reports AUROC 0.60, a gap beyond combined uncertainty (z = 3.97; balanced accuracy 0.835 against 0.60, z = 3.43), although the raw accuracies (83.3% and 74%) do not differ beyond uncertainty (z = 1.25); the differences in MRI features, sample size and validation, class balance, MCI composition and architecture are candidate explanations, none shown to be sufficient.
reason: z = 0.33/sqrt(0.0392^2 + 0.0734^2) = 3.97 (3.68 at a derived n of 60, 3.42 at 50). P-301's AUROC equals the balanced accuracy implied by its accuracy 0.74, kappa 0.25 and 32% AD share (sensitivity 0.21, specificity 0.99), so it looks hard-label. The like-for-like balanced-accuracy test also passes: 0.835 (SE 0.0534) against 0.60 (SE 0.0431), z = 3.43. Prevalence-dependent figures do not separate the papers: raw accuracy 0.833 against 0.74 gives z = 1.25, and P-152 reweighted to P-301's class mix gives 0.845, z = 1.40, because P-301 calls about 93% of a 68%-MCI set MCI. Source checks: P-301's Table 3 caption follows the DBN 0.74/0.60 block and matches its text; P-152's Table 3 MCI-AD row is 83.3/80.7/86.3/.93. Neither compared figure reaches 0.97. The record's own AD-vs-HC against AD-vs-MCI pairing is a misread and is set aside (condition 6). The pair came through the reader+skeptic route; the round-1 skeptic found no failed condition, so the full check was not repeated here. The result rests on a derived validation n for P-301.
candidate_explanations: Features within the MRI channel: superficial-white-matter DTI/tractography/connectivity features (P-152) against T1 regional volumes through 138 per-ROI 3D ViTs (P-301).

Sample size and validation: 48 subjects per contrast, with FCBF feature selection before an internal 5-fold CV and the best kernel reported (P-152), against a single 80/20 split of 364 AD+MCI (P-301).
Class balance and operating point: balanced 24/24 against 117 AD/247 MCI, with a derived AD sensitivity of about 0.21 and a hard-label-looking AUROC (P-301).
MCI composition: 140 of P-301's 247 MCI progress within 24 months; P-152 does not report its composition.
Cohort subset: ADNI2 DTI participants (P-152) against a baseline ADNI T1 dataset with two-year labels (P-301).
Architecture: kernel SVM against a DBN ensemble over 138 ROI vision transformers.

compared: MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, AUC of each paper's best model: P-178 9-feature RF (Table 4) against P-183 ENS on neuropsychology + T2-map imaging (Table 4, best AUC). No matched figure exists.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil on subject-level n: 95 test patients, about 12 converters (49 of 383 converted) and 83 non-converters: Q1 = 0.923, Q2 = 0.940, SE = sqrt([0.0384 + 11(0.0015) + 82(0.0188)]/996) = 0.0400 (visit level about 45/402: 0.0206).

one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, P-178 reports AUC 0.96 (early MCI, clinical scales plus hippocampal and ventricular volume, visit-level 95-patient test) and P-183 reports at best AUC 0.824 (95% CI 0.681-0.968; 40 patients, T2-map features plus neuropsychology), a difference not beyond combined uncertainty (z = 1.63), and P-178's higher accuracy (93.6% against 77.5%) comes from a test set that is 90% non-converters.
reason: z = 0.136/sqrt(0.0400^2 + 0.0732^2) = 1.63; 1.79 with visit-level n and 1.86 even with P-178's SE set to zero, so the test fails however n is taken. The advocate qualified the pair by the one-way test and by z = 2.39 against P-183's RF (0.770). The other models give 2.03 to 2.67. But P-183 names no primary model, and comparing P-178's best model with a weaker P-183 model is not neutral. Skeptic check: condition 1 holds; 2 holds; 3 holds on AUC but fails on accuracy (P-178's precision and recall, with the 90% non-converter share its SVC row fixes, give 0.788 at P-183's class mix against 0.775, and balanced accuracy 0.767 against 0.770-0.777; raw z = 2.15 only through the class mix); 4 fails under the uniform test; 5 holds (0.96 < 0.97, 383 patients); 6: the record's 'Acc 72.7' misreads P-183's neuropsychology-only LASSO AUC 0.727, so the pair is judged on the printed Table 4. The reader's verdict is upheld and the advocate's overturn is not.
candidate_explanations: Class prevalence (accuracy only): 90% non-converters in P-178's test against 45% converters in P-183; enough to explain the accuracy gap, but not AUC.

Evaluation unit and split: P-178 scores exam visits, and its Table 1 splits oversampled records 1206/402 per class, which reads as a record-level split, against the patient-level split its text describes.
Feature group chosen on test accuracy (P-178: removing RAVLT raised accuracy to 93.6%).
Population and horizon: early MCI labelled by last-visit diagnosis (5-7 years) against MCI aged 70-80 progressing at 2 years or stable for at least 5 years.
Features: ADAS13/ADAS11/FAQ/MMSE with hippocampal and ventricular volume (P-178) against neuropsychological scores with T2-map signal and texture features (P-183).
Sample size: 40 subjects in P-183.

compared: MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, held-out accuracy of each paper's best model: P-178 9-feature RF (Table 4) against P-212 ensemble on 139 held-out subjects ('the most accurate model'). No figure is printed under the other paper's condition, and P-212 reports no AUC.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial on 95 test patients: sqrt(0.936 x 0.064/95) = 0.0251.

b.se_source: No interval printed. 95/139 correct (20/74 sMCI and 24/65 cAD misclassified): sqrt(0.683 x 0.317/139) = 0.0395 (RF 92/139 = 0.662, SE 0.0401).

one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, P-178 reports 93.6% accuracy and P-212 68.3% on held-out data, but P-178's test set is 90% non-converters, and at P-212's class mix P-178's own class-wise figures give about 78% (balanced accuracy 0.77 against 0.68), a difference not beyond combined uncertainty (z = 1.24; 1.06 for balanced accuracy).
reason: Raw z = 0.253/0.0468 = 5.40 (5.79 against the RF), but the raw figures are not the same quantity. P-178's SVC row fixes its test set at 90% non-converters, so 0.936 is only 0.036 above its no-information rate. P-178's precision 0.952 and recall 0.978 give sensitivity 0.556 and specificity 0.978. At P-212's 46.8% converters that is 0.781 (SE 0.0676, about 12/83 test patients), against 0.683: z = 1.24 (1.51 against the RF). Balanced accuracy 0.767 (SE 0.0722) against 0.680 (SE 0.0395) gives z = 1.06 (1.31 against the RF). So P-178's own printed figures show the class mix is enough to bring the gap inside combined uncertainty, which is a paper showing an explanation sufficient: condition 3 fails. The first pass and the round-1 skeptic relied on a one-way exclusion (0.781 above 0.755), the test this round replaces. Caveats for the operator: per class, sensitivity agrees (z = 0.48) and specificity does not (0.978 against 0.730, z = 4.59), but specificity alone depends on the threshold; with visit-level n the balanced-accuracy z would be 1.60-1.97, but the brief requires subject-level n. Conditions 1, 2, 5 and 6 hold. The pair came through the reader+skeptic route, so the full skeptic check was not repeated.
candidate_explanations: Class prevalence and chance level: about 90% non-converters in P-178's test against 47% converters in P-212; P-178's own figures show this brings the gap inside combined uncertainty.
Diagnosis-defining scales as predictors in P-178 (ADAS13, ADAS11, FAQ, MMSE); P-212 excludes them because of circularity.
Population: early MCI only (P-178) against all ADNI MCI with at least three visits and MRIs (P-212).
Evaluation unit and oversampling: visit-level records with minority oversampling, and a Table 1 testing row (402/402) inconsistent with Table 4 (P-178).
Feature group chosen on test accuracy (P-178).
Validation: a single random 95-patient split against a stratified 139-subject held-out set after 50-fold CV (P-212 drops from 74.6% CV to 66.2% on test).
Overlapping ADNI participants, so the samples are not fully independent.

compared: Stable against progressive MCI in ADNI from baseline sMRI, AUC of each paper's reported model: P-185 linear SVM on the subspace biomarker against P-41 heterogeneous attention ensemble. No matched figure exists.

a.se_source: The +/-3.58 spread is not used as an SE. Hanley-McNeil with the 15 sMCI/15 pMCI+AD test subjects (Table 1 'Test 15 15'): Q1 = 0.867, Q2 = 0.894, SE = sqrt([0.0662 + 14(0.0044) + 14(0.0319)]/225) = 0.0505.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Hanley-McNeil with 126 pMCI/95 sMCI: Q1 = 0.533, Q2 = 0.570, SE = sqrt([0.2119 + 125(0.0495) + 94(0.0869)]/11970) = 0.0349.

one_sentence: For stable against progressive MCI from baseline structural MRI in ADNI, P-41 reports AUC 0.929 (accuracy 91.8%) on a 30-subject test and P-185 AUC 0.695 (accuracy 69.4%) on 221 subjects (z = 3.80), but P-41's own configurations without its attention module and ensemble score AUC 0.80-0.85 on the same test subjects, which does not differ from P-185 beyond combined uncertainty (z 1.14-1.85), so P-41's own ablation places the gap in architecture choices made on its test set.
reason: Headline z = 0.2336/0.0614 = 3.80 (accuracy 3.80; 2.81 at the 0.881 implied by P-41's own sensitivity and specificity). Skeptic check: conditions 1 (the 15 AD patients in the positive class are an allowed label difference), 2, 4 on the headline figures, 5 (0.929 < 0.97) and 6 hold. Condition 3 fails. The advocate's overturn used the one-way test, partly on printed accuracies that exceed both their own sensitivity and specificity, which is impossible on a 15/15 test. Under the uniform test, P-41's configurations without attention on the same 30 subjects do not differ from P-185 beyond combined uncertainty on AUC (ConvNext+LSTM coronal 0.8266, z = 1.55; DenseNet+LSTM axial 0.8454, z = 1.85, and 0.8054, z = 1.25; EfficientNet+MHA sagittal 0.7979, z = 1.14) or on the accuracies their sensitivity and specificity imply (z = 0.49-1.35). The gap passes only with attention on the best single model (AUC 0.8879, z = 2.68) and in the ensemble (z = 3.80), all chosen on the same test set. So the plain version of the method is within uncertainty of P-185. That is the C-147/C-155/C-117 convention, which the advocate itself accepted, and under it condition 3 fails. The reader's verdict stands. If the operator does not count a within-paper ablation under condition 3, the headline figures pass (z = 3.80).
candidate_explanations: Architecture and representation: an attention-augmented multi-plane CNN ensemble on 2D slices against a linear SVM on regional thickness and volume; P-41's configurations without attention or ensembling are within uncertainty of P-185.
Configuration selection on the test set: many backbone/head/plane combinations are scored on the same 30 test subjects and the best carried forward.
Label definition: 15 established AD patients are added to P-41's positive class.
Horizon: conversion within 3 years (P-185) against M18-M48 converters and M48 stables (P-41).
Test size and validation: a single 15 + 15 test against 20 x 10-fold CV on 221 MCI.
Field strength and phase: 1.5 T (P-185) against 3 T MPRAGE from ADNI 2 (P-41).
Reporting reliability: P-41's printed accuracies exceed both its sensitivity and its specificity throughout its tables.

compared: MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI MCI, accuracy with accuracy. There is no matched figure, so the headline figures are compared: P-203's printed conversion accuracy of 0.801 on its ADNI-2 test (the ledger's 91.1% is P-203's AD vs CN figure) against the ledger's P-212 figure, a random-forest held-out test accuracy of 0.662 (92/139). Against P-212's ensemble (0.683), z = 2.59.

a.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial sqrt(0.801 x 0.199/316) with n = 316 ADNI-2 MCI test subjects (75 pMCI / 241 sMCI, p.3; Table 4 p.6). ACC 0.801, SEN 0.520 and F1 0.553 fit one confusion matrix (TP 39, TN 214), which implies SPE 0.888. The printed SPE 0.856 is the inconsistent value, and the same holds in 3 of the other 4 rows.

b.se_source: No interval printed. Binomial sqrt(0.662 x 0.338/139) on the held-out test set, 'a test set comprising 21% (n = 139)' (p.8), with 'overall classification accuracy was 66.2%' (p.2). The 74.6-74.9% CV means come from the 50-fold hyperparameter search.

candidate_explanations: Class mix: 24% converters in P-203's test against 47% in P-212's. P-203's 0.801 is within uncertainty of its all-stable rate (0.763). Re-weighting closes the gap at P-212's mix but not at P-203's.
Operating threshold: P-203 runs at high specificity and low sensitivity; P-212 is near-symmetric. P-212 prints no AUC.
Label and horizon: conversion within 0-36 months against stability over 0-90 months (P-203), against conversion at any later visit (P-212).
Predictors: whole-brain T1 CNN against cognitive tests, hippocampal volume and APOE.
Validation: cross-phase ADNI-1 1.5 T to ADNI-2 3 T against an internal 79/21 split.
Reporting: P-203's SPE column does not fit its ACC, SEN and F1.
Both cohorts are ADNI, so participants may overlap.
None is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, a whole-brain MRI network reached 80.1% accuracy on a test set with 24% converters (P-203), while a cognitive-score, hippocampal-volume and APOE random forest reached 66.2% (ensemble 68.3%) on a test set with 47% converters (P-212). The gap is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 3.03), but the models agree on converters (sensitivity 0.52 vs 0.62-0.63) and differ only on stable MCI (specificity 0.86-0.89 vs 0.70-0.73), and P-203's figure is within uncertainty of its all-stable rate (76.3%).
reason: z = 0.139/sqrt(0.02246^2 + 0.04013^2) = 3.03, which passes (2.59 against the ensemble). The skeptic check could not show a failed condition. (1) The MRI channel is shared through P-212's FreeSurfer hippocampal volume, its top-ranked feature. (3) The per-class figures split: sensitivity agrees (z = 1.14-1.33), specificity does not (z = 2.85-3.26 on the implied value, 2.24-2.66 on the printed one). P-203 re-weighted to P-212's mix gives 0.716, which agrees (z = 0.66-1.09). P-212 re-weighted to P-203's mix gives 0.682-0.706 against 0.801, which disagrees (z = 1.99-2.45). The papers' own data therefore dissolve the gap in one direction only. (5) No figure reaches 0.97. (6) The record misreads P-203 (91.1%), but the gap persists on 0.801. Fragility: against P-212's tuning-CV means, z = 1.78-1.88, which fails.

compared: sMCI vs pMCI from T1 MRI in ADNI. There is no matched figure. The primary figure is ROC-AUC, 0.780 (P-3) vs 0.9287 (P-41), because P-41's printed accuracy of 91.77% exceeds both its sensitivity and its specificity on a balanced 15/15 test (and does so in 7 of 8 configurations). On accuracy, z = 3.22 on the printed figure and 2.19 on the 0.881 implied by P-41's sensitivity and specificity.

a.se_source: Only fold variances printed (Table row p.7). Hanley-McNeil with 295 pMCI / 298 sMCI (5-fold CV over 593, p.6): Q1 0.6393, Q2 0.6836, CI [0.743, 0.817].

b.se_source: Only run SDs printed (+/-3.58, p.12). Test set of 15 sMCI + 15 pMCI-or-AD subjects (Table 1 p.8). Hanley-McNeil 15/15: Q1 0.8669, Q2 0.8944, CI [0.830, 1.000].

candidate_explanations: Label definition: 15 AD patients were added to P-41's pMCI group. The test share is unstated. At the cohort share (2-3 of 15 test positives) the gap survives (z = 2.01-2.27); at 4 or more it would not.
Label window and possibly scan timepoint: converters between M18 and M48, and 'We specifically used pMCI subjects starting from M18' (P-41), against conversion within 36 months from baseline (P-3).
30 test subjects on which at least eight configurations were compared, against 5-fold CV over 593.
Input and architecture: multi-plane 2D slices in a CNN ensemble with CBAM and MHA, against a whole-3D-volume CNN with transferred attention.
Cohort: 192 ADNI 3 T subjects selected on data availability, against 593 subjects on the Wen et al. splits.
Reporting: P-41's accuracies are arithmetically impossible on a balanced test.
P-3 acknowledges tuning and selecting on the same CV, which would inflate P-3.
None is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For stable versus progressive MCI from T1 MRI in ADNI, a 3D attention-transfer CNN reached AUC 0.780 (accuracy 74.6%) in cross-validation over 593 subjects (P-3), while a 2D multi-plane CNN ensemble reached AUC 0.929 on a 30-subject test set whose progressive class included patients with established AD (P-41). Its printed accuracy of 91.8% is capped at 88.1% by its own sensitivity and specificity. The gap is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.76) but rests on 30 test subjects.
reason: z = 0.1487/sqrt(0.01896^2 + 0.05052^2) = 2.76, which passes (accuracy 2.19-3.22). The skeptic check could not show a failed condition. (1) P-41 frames its task as MCI progression, cites Luo et al. as prior work on the same problem, and compares with sMCI-vs-pMCI results; the AD admixture is a label-definition difference. The worst-case converter-only AUC bound gives z = 2.27 with k = 2, 2.01 with 3, 1.76 with 4 and 1.49 with 5 AD patients among the test positives. The expected k is 2.3, and the source does not state it, so the verdict depends on that split. (3) There is no matched figure. (5) No P-41 value reaches 97%. (6) The record's 'Acc 91' is the paper's own impossible figure, and the gap persists on the implied accuracy and on AUC.

compared: 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, ROC-AUC, with the cognitive channel shared. There is no matched figure (P-243 has no PET and no model without MRI volumes; P-81 has no sMRI model). P-243's test AUC of 0.89 is compared with P-81's PET + age + cognitive scores model (0.7849). Against P-81's CS + age model (0.8004), z = 2.24.

a.se_source: No CI printed for the test AUC (p.3). The test set is 30% of 627, about 188; the class split is not printed, so the cohort ratio 269/358 gives about 81/107. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 0.8018, Q2 0.8382, CI [0.839, 0.941]. Other plausible splits give z = 2.53-2.63.

b.se_source: Mean +/- fold SD 0.0963 (Table 3 p.4), treated as a spread. Hanley-McNeil with 93 unstable / 164 stable MCI (p.2): Q1 0.646, Q2 0.690, CI [0.723, 0.846].

candidate_explanations: P-81's figures are zero-shot predictions from a network trained on CN vs AD.
Cognitive instruments differ: FAQ, ADAS11, RAVLT and mPACCtrailsB in P-243, against CDR-SB, LDEL, MMSE and mPACC in P-81.
Imaging channel: MRI volumes against FDG-PET, which P-81 shows adds little.
Cohort selection: 3-year follow-up required and bidirectional changes excluded in P-243, against a PET-within-two-months requirement in P-81; class balance 43% vs 36% converters.
Model selection among nine models with a 30% held-out test (P-243), against 5-fold CV with a fold SD of 0.096 (P-81).
Both cohorts are ADNI, so participants may overlap.
None is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI, AdaBoost on cognitive scores and three MRI volumes reached AUC 0.89 on a held-out test set of about 188 (P-243), while a zero-shot network on FDG-PET, age and cognitive scores reached AUC 0.785 in cross-validation over 257 (P-81; 0.800 without PET). The gap is beyond combined uncertainty (z = 2.59), and instruments, imaging channel, training regime, cohort selection and validation are untested candidate explanations.
reason: z = 0.1051/sqrt(0.02578^2 + 0.03138^2) = 2.59, which passes, and the result is robust to P-243's test split (2.53-2.63). No full skeptic check was required; challenge_skeptic_6 found no failed condition, and the figures were re-checked on P-243 pp.2-3 and P-81 pp.2 and 4. No compared figure is near ceiling. The ledger's P-320 label is a record defect: the figure is P-81's.

compared: Time to MCI-to-AD conversion, Harrell's C on an internal hold-out, with the clinical and cognitive channel shared. Matched by model family: RSF 0.878 (P-344) vs RSF 0.781 (P-309). Cox vs Cox gives z = 2.23, and best vs best (0.878 vs 0.798) gives z = 2.85. The ledger's claimed reversal of the RSF-versus-Cox ordering is not decidable, because it needs a between-model correlation neither paper reports.

a.se_source: The printed bootstrap CI 0.877-0.879 (p.5) is too narrow to be a sampling interval for n = 271, so the SE is derived (the printed CI would give z = 5.69). The test set of 271 is stratified with 42.0% events (p.4-5), about 114/157. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 0.7825, Q2 0.8210, CI [0.833, 0.923].

b.se_source: No CI printed (p.1). The validation set is 30% of 3,674, about 1,102, with about 27% events (p.2), about 298/804. Hanley-McNeil: Q1 0.6407, Q2 0.6850, CI [0.748, 0.814].

candidate_explanations: Imaging predictors: FDG-PET and four MRI volumes in P-344, none in P-309.
Cohort: ADNI research cohort against NACC memory-clinic data with investigator diagnoses.
Follow-up: up to 16 years (median time to progression 6 years) against a median of 24.5 months; P-309 shows discrimination falling with horizon.
Event rate: 42.0% against about 27%.
P-344's imputation and Lasso-Cox selection are described before the split, so its test figure may be optimistic.
Different cognitive instruments within the channel.
Test size: 271 against about 1,102.
None is shown to be sufficient.
one_sentence: For time to MCI-to-AD conversion, a random survival forest reached a C-index of 0.878 on a 271-subject ADNI test set with imaging, genetic and cognitive predictors (P-344), against 0.781 (Cox 0.798) on about 1,102 NACC validation subjects with clinical and cognitive predictors only (P-309). The level differs beyond combined uncertainty (z = 3.42; Cox vs Cox 2.23), but the ledger's claimed reversal of which model ranks best cannot be decided from either paper.
reason: z = 0.097/sqrt(0.02272^2 + 0.01703^2) = 3.42, which passes; Cox gives 2.23 and best vs best 2.85. Hanley-McNeil only approximates Harrell's C under censoring: the RSF result holds unless both SEs are more than 1.74 times the derived values, and the Cox result tolerates only 1.14 times. No full skeptic check was required; challenge_skeptic_6 found no failed condition, and the sizes and event rates were re-checked on P-344 pp.4-5 and P-309 pp.1-2 and 5. The pair qualifies on the absolute C-index, not on the ordering claim.

compared: MCI against community controls from plasma exosomal RNA, headline in-sample AUCs (no matched figure exists: neither paper measures the other's markers or reports a result under the other's case definition or control group). P-1254 miR-483-5p 0.901 (24 v 24 age-matched) against P-1232 three-lncRNA logistic combination 0.700 (150 v 150). P-1254's miR-502-5p (0.872) checked as well.

a.se_source: No CI printed: 'miR-483-5p showed an AUC of 0.901' on '24 MCI patients and 24 age-matched controls' (pp. 2, 4-5). Hanley-McNeil 24/24: Q1 0.8198, Q2 0.8541, SE^2 = 1.2465/576, SE 0.0465 (miR-502-5p 0.872: SE 0.0527).

candidate_explanations: Different analytes: a three-lncRNA logistic panel (P-1232) against single miRNAs (P-1254); each study measures only its own markers. This is the leading candidate.
Marker preselection and in-sample optimism in P-1254: four literature candidates, ROC reported only for the two that separated the groups, 48 people, no CI, cross-validation or external cohort.
Sample size: 24 v 24 against 150 v 150.
Control group: P-1254's 'age-matched' controls average 73.35 years against 78.12 for MCI, and 'CD9 showed an increasing trend dependent on age'; P-1232's controls are matched 1:1.
Label definition: education-specific MMSE cut-offs (P-1232) against MoCA < 26 plus European Consortium criteria (P-1254).
Cohort: Guangzhou community case-control sample against a Gansu community survey.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: Two community studies using plasma exosomal RNA to separate Chinese older adults with MCI from controls report AUCs that differ beyond their combined uncertainty: P-1254 reports 0.901 for miR-483-5p, in-sample, in 24 v 24 people, and P-1232 reports 0.700 (95% CI 0.641-0.760) for a three-lncRNA panel in 150 v 150 (z = 3.62). The studies measure different markers, which is the leading candidate explanation; P-1254's in-sample estimate after marker selection, its younger controls, the MCI definitions and the cohorts are others, and none is shown to be sufficient.
reason: No matched figure exists. z = 3.62 on the headline AUCs and 2.83 on P-1254's weaker marker (|0.872-0.700|/sqrt(0.0527^2+0.0304^2)), so the gap exceeds combined uncertainty. The first-round skeptic upheld conditions 1-3, 5 and 6, and the source re-reading agrees: both AUCs are below 0.97 and in-sample, and P-1254's ROC is the 24 v 24 age-matched contrast. The pair qualifies, with the different-analyte caveat.

compared: Agreement between data-driven neuropsychological classification and consensus MCI/NC diagnosis in ADRC participants, headline concordance (no matched figure exists). P-955: LCA against consensus, 90% of 354. P-1084: Ward clusters against NACC consensus, 65.4%, derived from its Table 2 restricted to consensus NC and MCI (P-955's frame). P-955's actuarial concordance of 84% checked as well.

a.se_source: No CI printed: 'concordant diagnoses for 90% of cases' (p. 9), N = 354 (p. 1). Binomial sqrt(0.9 x 0.1/354) = 0.0159.

scale: proportion (raw concordance); kappa 0.80 v 0.34 reported, not tested
candidate_explanations: Normative reference: robust-CN norms (P-1084) against published norms (P-955); 'Robust norms may create a higher standard for normal' (P-1084). Neither paper tests this.
Sampling frame: one ADRC against the multi-site NACC UDS ('the previous study was conducted in a sample of participants from one ADRC', P-1084).
Reference label: NACC consensus 'appeared to be heavily driven by CDR scores' (P-1084), while P-955's consensus used comprehensive neuropsychological data.
Impairment threshold: 'This difference in the definition of what constitutes memory impairment may have contributed to more participants being classified with MCI' (P-1084).
Algorithm and input: LCA on domain scores (P-955) against Ward clustering on individual test z scores (P-1084).
Battery differences (14 measures including CERAD against a UDS subset).
Independence caveat: the Penn ADRC contributes to NACC, so the samples may partly overlap.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: In Alzheimer's Disease Research Center participants, data-driven classification from neuropsychological tests agreed with the consensus MCI/normal diagnosis for 90% of 354 people in P-955 (latent class analysis, one centre, kappa 0.80), but for 65.4% of 24,518 in P-1084 (hierarchical clustering, NACC; derived from its Table 2, kappa 0.34), a gap far beyond combined uncertainty (z = 15.1). P-1084 names the contrast itself. Robust-normal norms, one centre against many, a CDR-driven consensus, the impairment threshold and the algorithm are candidate explanations that neither paper tests.
reason: No matched figure exists. z = 15.1 on headline concordance, and P-955's actuarial rule, the closest in impairment definition, still gives z = 9.41 against P-1084 (0.84, SE 0.0195). The first-round skeptic upheld conditions 1-3, 5 and 6; the counts check out against the sources. The pair qualifies.

compared: Difference in reversion between conventional/Petersen and Jak/Bondi NP MCI criteria (conventional minus NP), matched to P-1136's definitions. P-986: Petersen with relaxed follow-up (42.1%, n 1063) minus original NP without complaint (54.7%, n 528) = -0.126. P-1136: full-sample Table 3, 192/325 = 59.1% minus 246/531 = 46.3% = +0.128. The headline figures and all other pairings were checked.

a.se_source: Printed Table 2 CIs (p. 9): 42.1% (39.1; 45.1) and 54.7% (50.4; 59.0); SEs 0.0153 and 0.0219; SE of the difference, treating the samples as independent (conservative, because they overlap), = 0.0268.

b.se_source: No CI printed. Table 3 (p. 5): reverters/consistent 192/133 (conventional) and 246/285 (NP); binomial SE of the difference = sqrt(0.591 x 0.409/325 + 0.463 x 0.537/531) = 0.0348.

scale: difference in proportions (reversion, conventional minus NP)
candidate_explanations: Age window and cohort: InveCe.Ab enrolled ages 70-74 at baseline; GAS/SNAC pooled samples aged 60 and over.
Complaint prevalence, which the conventional rule requires, was 'probably lower than that in the clinical setting' in P-1136 (conventional MCI 18.5% against 43.8% under NP).
Education: low and heterogeneous in InveCe.Ab (mean 7.2 years).

Stability definition: P-1136 counts impairment-only persistence and keeps progressors; P-986 requires complaint and ADL of reverters and excludes progressors. Both parts were tested approximately, and the gap stays.
Same-participant frame differs (P-986 n = 334 with data for both criteria; P-1136 280 with MCI under both).
Follow-up cadence: every 3 or 6 years against waves at 0, 2, 4, 8 and 12 years.
Norms: external SNAC norms against internal InveCe.Ab norms.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: Two population cohorts disagree on which MCI criteria give the more stable diagnosis. In P-986 (Sweden), Petersen MCI reverts to normal no more often than Jak/Bondi MCI (43.4% against 48.3%; 42.1% against 54.7% under P-1136's rules). In P-1136 (Italy), conventional MCI reverts more often (59.1% against 46.3% overall; 56.8% against 36.8% in the same 280 people). The difference exceeds combined uncertainty on the matched contrast (z = 5.77) and is at least 3.39 in every pairing. The age window, complaint prevalence, education, follow-up schedule and norms are candidate explanations, and none is shown to be sufficient.
reason: The orderings are opposite. z = 5.77 matched, 5.48 on the headlines (P-986 -0.049, SE 0.0321, against P-1136's paired +0.200, SE 0.0321 from McNemar b+c = 92), and 3.39 on the most conservative pairing (P-986 impairment-only -0.020 against P-1136 with progressors removed +0.129). The first-round skeptic upheld conditions 1-3, 5 and 6, and P-1136 names the contrast with P-986 itself. The pair qualifies.

compared: Share of people with dementia diagnosed in high-income systems, headline figures (no matched figure exists): P-1046 US Medicare dementia O/E 1.086 (lowest of 1.086-1.104) against P-977's 'In most HIC, only 40-50% ... have received a diagnosis' (midpoint 0.45); P-977's sourced 37.9% (26.8-49.6%) checked as well.

a.se_source: No CI printed. Claims sampling SE is negligible (0.00005 on 38.7M). Model-denominator SE from the HRS validation (observed dementia 0.078, N = 9,808): 0.00271, a relative 3.47%, so 1.086 x 0.0347 = 0.0377.

b.se_source: No source, n or CI is printed for the headline (p. 12; its attached refs 3-5 are LMIC studies), so the brief's SE cannot be derived. The range treated as if it were a 95% interval gives 0.10/3.92 = 0.0255. Check: 37.9% (26.8-49.6%) gives SE 0.0582, z = 10.20.

scale: proportion diagnosed against an observed/expected ratio: not the same quantity
candidate_explanations: Metric construction: O/E counts every coded diagnosis, including those P-1046 calls overdiagnosis ('detection rate 1.23, suggesting a 23% rate of overdiagnosis'); coverage counts only diagnosed true cases.
Observed rate accumulated 'over rolling windows of 3 years', including decedents, against a point-in-time expected prevalence.
Expected-rate denominator 0.086 is below the Rajan (0.113) and Manly (0.100) estimates the paper cites.
A demographics-only model 'has only adequate accuracy'.
Population and era: US Medicare 2015-2019 against a generic 'most HIC' figure whose attached references are LMIC studies.
P-977's sourced evidence comes from primary-care attenders given a research assessment.
These would need weighing only if the figures measured one quantity, and they do not.
one_sentence: P-1046's US Medicare dementia detection ratio (claims-coded diagnoses over model-expected prevalence, 1.086-1.104 in 2015-2019) and P-977's statement that only 40-50% of people with dementia in most high-income countries have a diagnosis are far apart numerically (z about 14), but they do not measure the same thing. P-1046 counts every coded diagnosis and itself reads its ratio above 1 as overdiagnosis, so the ratio puts no bound on the share of true cases diagnosed, and P-977's figure has no source, sample or interval. The pair is therefore not an unresolved discrepancy.
reason: The z test passes on every construction (13.97; 10.20; 4.04 for P-1046's lowest subgroup), but the skeptic check finds condition 2 fails on the sources. O/E = coverage + coded non-cases/expected cases, and P-1046 reads the excess over 1 as overdiagnosis ('overdiagnosed ... by about 10%'), so 1.086 is compatible with any coverage, depending on an unmeasured false-positive share. The advocate's reliance on the authors' interpretive sentence and their comparison with 38% and 62% does not change the estimator. Condition 1 holds only loosely (P-977's figure is unsourced and its attached references are LMIC studies). Conditions 3 and 5 hold. For condition 6, the record's quote 'underestimates true prevalence' is not in P-1046, but the printed numbers are as stated. The pair does not qualify.

compared: Antihypertensive use against none and progression from MCI to dementia, adjusted Cox HR, on the matched contrast: P-999 'any AHM users vs AHM non-users' (Table 3) against P-1157's pooled 'Antihypertensive Drugs' category. P-999's per-class figures (a different contrast) and its statin and metformin strata (not P-1157's condition) are reported as sensitivity. The record's pairing (per-class 0.96-0.98 against polypharmacy 0.49) compares different factors and is not used.

a.se_source: Log scale, from the printed 95% CI. Table 3 (p. 13) 'Users vs. Non-users 1.06 (1.04, 1.08) < 0.001'; p. 14 'Patients who use any form of AHMs had 6% higher adjusted hazard ratio of ADRD (95% CI: (1.04, 1.08), P < 0.001)'. N = 128,683 (100,678 vs 28,005). SE = (ln 1.08 - ln 1.04)/3.92 = 0.00963; ln 1.06 = 0.05827.

b.se_source: Log scale, from the printed 95% CI. p. 5 'antihypertensive agents (HR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.37 to 0.93)'; N = 237, 89 progressed; all models adjusted for the same covariates (p. 4). SE = (ln 0.93 - ln 0.37)/3.92 = 0.2351; ln 0.59 = -0.52763.

candidate_explanations: Population and reference group: P-999 is restricted to hypertensive MCI, so its comparator is untreated hypertensives, and it excluded normotensives because hypertension status 'could not be well controlled'. P-1157 includes normotensives and has no hypertension covariate; its progressors had less hypertension (p = 0.003). Crude progression is 30.5% (47/154) in hypertensives against 50.6% (42/83) in normotensives, a ratio of 0.60, close to the HR of 0.59.

Co-medication: P-999 adjusts for statin and metformin use, and its any-AHM estimate reverses with statin co-use (0.84 with, 1.11 without). P-1157's per-category models adjust for no other drug, and lipid-modifying agents are separately protective there (HR 0.43).
Exposure window: baseline prescription records (P-1157) against use 'during the study period' (P-999).
Outcome ascertainment: claims-based ADRD (P-999) against CDR 0.5 to 1, confirmed by neurologists (P-1157).
Setting and size: US Optum claims, N = 128,683 (a preprint), against Taiwanese veterans' homes and a hospital outpatient clinic, N = 237.
Multiplicity: P-1157's estimate is one of 15 exploratory per-category models, tested at p < 0.05 without correction.
Neither paper shows any of these to be sufficient.
one_sentence: Two cohort studies of older adults with MCI disagree on antihypertensive use and progression to dementia.
